title: 【Health】L'initiative du village de Sawauchi, fondateur au Japon de la mortalité infantile zéro
text:
【Health】L'initiative du village de Sawauchi, fondateur au Japon de la mortalité infantile zéro
La JICA offre à ses boursiers qui suivent des programmes de maîtrise ou de doctorat dans des établissements d'enseignement supérieur japonais diverses possibilités de se familiariser avec l'histoire locale japonaise et les expériences de développement dans le cadre du programme d'études sur le développement de la JICA.Cette vidéo a été produite par la JICA Tohoku dans le cadre du programme d'études sur le développement de la JICA.

Le village de Sawauchi, dans la préfecture d'Iwate, avait le taux de mortalité infantile le plus élevé du Japon. La neige abondante, la pauvreté et les problèmes de santé publique sont autant de problèmes qui s'y posent.
Pourtant, ce village, décrit autrefois comme une sorte de cage de neige, a atteint un taux de mortalité infantile nul en 1962. La question est de savoir comment.
Cette vidéo présente ce que signifie être humain en montrant les efforts déployés pour atteindre le taux zéro de mortalité infantile et comment cette réussite a changé le sentiment d'accomplissement des gens.

title: 【Health】Initiative of Sawauchi small village, the founder in Japan achieved zero infant mortality
text:
【Health】Initiative of Sawauchi small village, the founder in Japan achieved zero infant mortality
JICA offers its scholars in master’s or doctoral programs at Japanese graduate schools various opportunities to learn about Japanese local history and development experiences as part of the JICA Development Studies Program.This video was produced by JICA Tohoku as part of the Program.

Sawauchi-mura, a small village in Iwate Prefecture suffered from high infant mortality rate in a challenging circumstance of heavy snow, poverty, and low public health services.
Yet, the village, which was once described as a snow-cage-like place, achieved the zero infant mortality rate in 1962 as Japan's first. The question is how.
This video introduces potentials of the poeple through showing the efforts to achieve the zero infant mortality rate and how this achievement changed people's sense of fulfillment.

title: 【Republica Dominicana・Salud】Artist in Project「Vamo Chequeo」Cancion de prevención
text:
【Republica Dominicana・Salud】Artist in Project「Vamo Chequeo」Cancion de prevención
Artistas en Proyecto (AIP), una nueva propuesta de proyecto en la JICA, trabaja para desarrollar nuevos contenidos de cooperación y proponer la próxima generación de cooperación internacional trabajando con artistas desde la perspectiva del arte y la cultura. Al incorporar los métodos de expresión y los mensajes de los artistas en el ámbito de la  Cooperación Internacional, AIP pretende conseguir un desarrollo más atractivo e innovador mediante la creación de un «contenido simpático, simple» que sea más atractivo y más fácil de entender. 


A partir de 2023, la JICA está ejecutando el Proyecto de Fortalecimiento de la Atención Primaria de Salud para la Prevención y Gestión de Enfermedades No Transmisibles, un proyecto de cooperación técnica para combatir enfermedades no transmisibles tales como: la diabetes y la hipertensión. (https://www.jica.go.jp/oda/project/202108766/index.html)

En colaboración con este proyecto, se produjo la canción 'VamoChequeo' como subproyecto de AIP para concienciar sobre la importancia de los chequeos médicos en la República Dominicana. Los almuerzos escolares y la educación alimentaria en función de la Salud del planeta: para los niños y para un futuro sostenible

School Meals and Shokuiku in Japan Through the Lens of Planetary Health:For the Children,and a Sustainable Future(Spanish Full version)

In recent years, due to the extreme heat caused by global warming, the price of vegetables has been rising, and as a result, it has become evident that our diet is closely connected to climate change. It is also said that around 30% of greenhouse gases are caused by the food system. In this way, in the context of climate change, the concept of 'Planetary Health' refers to the inter-relationship between 'health of the planet' and 'health of human beings’ and trying to solve this problem in a practical way. 

School meals and Shokuiku (Food and nutrition education) can be said to be a tangible example of 'Planetary Health'. In recent years, due to the extreme heat caused by global warming, the price of vegetables has been rising, and as a result, it has become evident that our diet is closely connected to climate change. It is also said that around 30% of greenhouse gases are caused by the food system. In this way, in the context of climate change, the concept of 'Planetary Health' refers to the inter-relationship between 'health of the planet' and 'health of human beings’ and trying to solve this problem in a practical way. 

School meals and Shokuiku (Food and nutrition education) can be said to be a tangible example of 'Planetary Health'. By bringing the local communities together, including local government, nutrition professionals, cooks, schools, farmers and children, community-based delicious school meals can be realized, and as a result, this can be not only an 'adaptation measure' but also a 'mitigation measure' for climate change.

text:
Seminar “State-Managed International Voluntary Service: The Case of JOCV” [JICA]
Recently, the JICA Ogata Research Institute published the book “State-Managed International Voluntary Service: The Case of Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCVs)” as the final deliverable of the research project “Contributions of International Volunteers in Bringing Change to Developing Countries and Shaping a Global Civil Society,” with Professor Okabe Yasunobu, Tohoku University, as the editor. In this book, the concept of state-managed international voluntary services (SMIVS) is proposed, the contribution of JOCVs to both downstream and upstream benefits is analyzed and the strengths and weaknesses of SMIVS are discussed. 

In this seminar, Okabe shared an overview of this book. After that, the authors of this book, both researchers and practitioners, will join a discussion on the book, particularly on its academic significance and the practical suggestions made.

text:
JICA Video :History of international cooperation in the field of maritime safety and security
Japan's international cooperation in the field of maritime safety and security began in the late 1960s with efforts for maritime traffic safety in Southeast Asia. Afterwards, it has broadened to sea rescue and oil spill response. In recent years, the nature of cooperation has further expanded from the previous "safety" to "security" including maritime law enforcement and maintenance of maritime order based on international law.

This video material provides an insight into the history of international cooperation in the field of maritime safety and security.

title: Building Hope in Ukraine #6 Supporting railways for emergency recovery
text:
Building Hope in Ukraine #6 Supporting railways for emergency recovery
JICA is providing emergency assistance with the aim of rapid recovery and reconstruction of Ukraine. Ukraine's railway network suffered extensive damage and, Ukraine lost its capacity of production of rails as iron and steel works is incapable.
With JICA's cooperation, 192 km of railway rails have been provided to Ukrainian Railways, which are being laid on the damaged lines.
During wartime with the airspace closed, railways became vital "lifeline" connecting people and sustaining logistics both domestically and internationally. Today the railways continue to run strong on the provided rails, undeterred by the flames of war.

title: JICA Indonesia: Empowering Women Micro-Entrepreneurs Through Digital Skills
text:
JICA Indonesia: Empowering Women Micro-Entrepreneurs Through Digital Skills
Under the JICA Partnership Project, Kopernik together with the local counterpart,‘Aisyiyah, one of the largest Islamic women's organizations in Indonesia, supported Indonesian women micro-entrepreneurs in launching or improving online businesses that can be operated from home, addressing challenges of limited face-to-face sales due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

This project titled “Capacity Development of Online Sales Skills to Women Support Group and Women Micro Entrepreneurs to Increase Livelihood” started in August 2021 and ended in July 2024. The project trained seven facilitators, who train women micro entrepreneurs, and twenty-four women micro entrepreneurs, equipping them with essentials skills for online business development including finance, marketing, branding and photography,  online store set-up and online sales, business monitoring & consultation, and social media establishment practice.

title: JICA Indonesia: Capacity Improvement for Sustainable System on Maintenance of RO Membrane Filtration
text:
JICA Indonesia: Capacity Improvement for Sustainable System on Maintenance of RO Membrane Filtration
Messah Island in West Manggarai has been struggling with a shortage of domestic water supply. For years, local people relied on purchasing water from Labuan Bajo and nearby islands. The daily needs of 20 to 40 liters incurs significant costs due to boat transport.

Under JICA Partnership program, Toyama Prefectural University is addressing this challenge with project “Support Project for Capacity Improvement, Establishment of Sustainable System on Maintenance of RO Membrane Filtration System in Messah Island.”  

The project introduced a reverse osmosis (RO) membrane filtration system to provide clean and affordable water to the community. In addition to installing and operating the filtration system, the project established a local association that consist of twenty members to maintain and manage the system.

title: In Palau With Takanashi Sara - Realizing a Sustainable Society
text:
In Palau With Takanashi Sara - Realizing a Sustainable Society
Ski jumper Takanashi Sara has been learning about climate change and taking part in activities to protect snow-covered mountains, as she feels a sense of crisis that the next generation of children may not be able to enjoy snow sports due to the lack of snow caused by global warming. 

Sara visited the Republic of Palau, an island nation in the Pacific Ocean. 
Palau is blessed with its beautiful World Heritage-listed coastal ecosystems, including its oceans, forests, coral reefs and mangroves. However, it also faces problems such as the the disposal of waste caused by typhoons and due to the development of its tourism industry. It is important to improve the sanitary environment and conserve the natural environment by properly disposing of waste in a limited land area.

In addition, initiatives are being promoted towards a recycling-oriented society, such as the promotion of recycling activities by residents and the operation of a glass studio that uses energy generated from waste.

In this video, you will learn about Palau's efforts to realize a Sustainable Society, together with JICA.

title: Interview“Exploring Human Security and Development Practice" with Professor Sachiko Ishikawa　[JICA]
text:
Interview“Exploring Human Security and Development Practice" with Professor Sachiko Ishikawa　[JICA]
Professor Sachiko Ishikawa of Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto, is co-editor of the book "Human Security and Empowerment in Asia" and has studied how the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) was involved in the peace process in Mindanao in the Philippines. In this interview, she mentions that Japan’s assistance to Mindanao was from the onset, based on the goal of achieving human security and that measuring the human security impact of development projects is difficult because it cannot be measured quantitatively, but by picking up as many voices and stories from the field as possible, we can clarify the contours of the impact.

The book reports the results of a research project titled “Human Security and the Practices of Empowerment in East Asia” conducted by the JICA Ogata Research Institute for Peace and Development.

title: 【Nutrition】School Meals and Shokuiku in Japan through the lens of Planetary Health(Digest ver.)
text:
【Nutrition】School Meals and Shokuiku in Japan through the lens of Planetary Health(Digest ver.)
In recent years, due to the extreme heat caused by global warming, the price of vegetables has been rising, and as a result, it has become evident that our diet is closely connected to climate change. It is also said that around 30% of greenhouse gases are caused by the food system. In this way, in the context of climate change, the concept of 'Planetary Health' refers to the inter-relationship between 'health of the planet' and 'health of human beings’ and trying to solve this problem in a practical way. 

School meals and Shokuiku (Food and nutrition education) can be said to be a tangible example of 'Planetary Health'. By bringing the local communities together, including local government, nutrition professionals, cooks, schools, farmers and children, community-based delicious school meals can be realized, and as a result, this can be not only an 'adaptation measure' but also a 'mitigation measure' for climate change. 

This video, through the example of Fukuroi City in Shizuoka Prefecture and commentary from experts, explains the characteristics and main points of school lunches and food education in Japan, particularly from the perspective of climate change. We hope that people in countries that are introducing or improving school meals will find this video useful. 〈This is the 7 min. digest version 〉

title: Erbil 2050 Master Plan towards Sustainable City Development
text:
Erbil 2050 Master Plan towards Sustainable City Development
The city of Erbil, under the jurisdiction of the Kurdistan Regional Government(KRG), plays a crucial role in economic development and connectivity of this region of Iraq. In recent years, urbanization in Erbil has rapidly accelerated,leading to significant challenges such as water scarcity, vulnerability to flooding or car dependency. 
To address these challenges and ensure a sustainable and low-carbon urban growth in the future, the Project to update the Erbil Master Plan was conducted under the supervision of the General Directorate of Urban Planning (GDUP) of the Ministry of Municipalities & Tourism (MoMT) with the support of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). It is expected that the urban infrastructure of Erbil will be developed in the future utiilzing this Master Plan.

Brochure of the Erbil 2050 Master Plan:

title: Developing countries’ officials meet artists with disabilities @ HERALBONY & Lumbini Art Museum!
text:
Developing countries’ officials meet artists with disabilities @ HERALBONY & Lumbini Art Museum!
JICA aims to create an inclusive and sustainable society in which all people can meaningfully participate with equity regardless of their gender, age, culture, social and economic status and disability.
As a part to achieve this, JICA has started a co-creation program with HERALBONY Co., Ltd. since April 2024. With "Radiate your Color" as the company’s mission, HERALBONY manages the licensing of art data created by artists, primarily those with intellectual disabilities, both in Japan and internationally, while expanding a variety of businesses. HERALBONY and JICA aim to transform the image of disability in Japan and developing countries to realize a society where people with and without disabilities can live their lives in their own way.

In August 2024, JICA invited officials from developing countries to Japan and conducted a knowledge co-creation program on the theme of ‘Promotion of Social Participation of Persons with Disabilities through Sports’. During the program, participants visited the Lumbini Art Museum in Hanamaki City, Iwate Prefecture, where they interacted with artists contracted by HERALBONY, as well as related parties at HERALBONY’s head office in Morioka City. After the explanations of Lumbini Art Museum and HERALBONY’s initiatives, the participants actively exchanged views on efforts towards art activities and social participation by people with disabilities.

title: Knowledge Forum“Historical Overview and Future Perspectives of Japan’s Development Cooperation”
text:
Knowledge Forum“Historical Overview and Future Perspectives of Japan’s Development Cooperation”
The year 2024 marks the 70th anniversary since Japan started providing official development assistance (ODA) to developing countries. Based on its own experience and knowledge, Japan has long worked to build a peaceful and stable international society by supporting developing countries to lay the foundation for development. Over the last 70 years, there have also been recipient countries that have become donor countries, including China, Thailand and Malaysia.

On the other hand, recent issues of natural disasters and extreme weather events due to climate change have given rise to problems such as food crises. Further issues that have arisen since 2020 include the COVID-19 pandemic, the invasion of Ukraine by Russia, and conflicts between Israeli and Palestinian armed groups, and global issues and rifts between people and regions are worsening. In particular, developing countries without robust social infrastructure are unable to handle such global risks.The situation continues to grow in severity in combination with structural issues, such as poverty and social customs. What can Japan’s development cooperation do as the international society faces such compounded crises that threaten human security? What lessons can be found for the future by looking back on the history of development cooperation through to today?

title: Blue Transition with Deep Ocean Water
text:
Blue Transition with Deep Ocean Water
Many island countries are vulnerable to climate change. For example and water shortages due to droughts are becoming more frequent. Many island nations rely on diesel generators for electricity, but energy prices are high due to transportation costs. In many island nations, industries are limited to agriculture, fisheries, and tourism. In Kumejima, Kumejima Town, Saga University, and private companies have been working together to conduct a demonstration project for 10 years. By using deep ocean water in cascade use, the project provides not only clean electricity, but also drinking water and industries such as aquaculture and cosmetics. JICA belives that the Kumejima model will be a game changer that contributes to mitigation and adaptation measures for many countries. JICA is challenging the expansion of the Kumejima model with many partners, developing countries, private companies, adademia and public institutions.
多くの島嶼国は気候変動に脆弱であり、干ばつによる水不足の頻度が増加しています。多くの島嶼国は電力をディーゼル発電機に頼っていますが、輸送費がかかるため、エネルギーの料金は高い状況にあります。多くの島嶼国は産業が農業や水産業、観光業に限られています。久米島では、久米島町と佐賀大学、民間企業が連携し10年間実証事業が継続しています。海洋深層水の多段利用により、クリーンな電力のみならず、飲料水や養殖などの産業を提供しています。久米島モデルは多くの島嶼国にとって緩和策と適応策に貢献するゲームチェンジャーになると期待しています。JICAは途上国、民間企業、大学・研究機関、公的機関等の多くのパートナーと共に久米島モデルの拡大に挑戦しています。

title: Seminar "Accelerating Actions Toward SDGs and Human Security: The Summit of the Future and Beyond"
text:
Seminar "Accelerating Actions Toward SDGs and Human Security: The Summit of the Future and Beyond"
Threats such as climate change, armed conflict, pandemics, natural disasters, and economic crises are intertwined in complex ways, resulting in ever more serious and pervasive crises. In light of the ever-changing global situation, the UN Secretary-General's Report on Human Security, published in January 2024, highlights the significance of human security as “a tool to accelerate the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals.”

The Summit of the Future in September 2024 at the UN was a landmark event for discussing how international cooperation could effectively achieve agreed goals and tackle emerging threats and opportunities. The summit focused on “how” to achieve it, not “what” to achieve - calling for concrete actions to deliver a better present and safeguard our prosperous future.

In this online symposium, Mine Yoichi, Executive Director of the JICA Ogata Research Institute, gave a keynote speech on the significance of human security in an era of complex global development landscape, based on the insights of “Human Security Today No.2”  published by the JICA Ogata Research Institute in September 2024. In the following panel discussion, prominent speakers discussed how best to “accelerate the achievement of the SDGs” through human security perspectives.

title: JICA Gabon:le programme des volontaires Japonais et leurs activités
text:
JICA Gabon:le programme des volontaires Japonais et leurs activités
Créé en 1965 le programme des JOCV, entendez « Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers » a pour principaux objectifs, de contribuer au développement socio-économique du pays d’accueil, de renforcer l’amitié mutuelle entre les deux pays et de redonner l’expérience du volontariat à la société. Au Gabon c’est en 2005, que le bureau de la Jica a vu ses six premiers volontaires arrivés. Les volontaires de la JICA dit JOCV participent au développement d’un pays par le transfert de compétences : ils partagent leur savoir-faire dans des domaines variés tel que la santé, l’éducation, la pêche, le développement communautaire et social, la préservation de l’environnement ou encore le sport. Ils s’imprègnent également des cultures locales en partageant leur quotidien mais surtout en vivant dans le même environnement que les peuples autochtones. Près de 20 ans plus tard après son lancement, grâce à la JICA et son programme, ce sont plus de 200 volontaires japonais qui ont pu partager leurs connaissances et expériences acquises avec leurs homologues Gabonais.
Ce court métrage vous fera découvrir le programme des JOCV, son histoire, le processus de recrutement et d’affectation mais plus particulièrement les multiples interventions et activités des volontaires japonais au Gabon dans différents secteurs.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 5 Holiday Inn Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
text:
Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 5 Holiday Inn Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
In Mongolia, legal systems are being developed to guarantee the rights of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and promote their social participation. What changes will be made to PWDs and companies when working in companies? What considerations are required?
DPUB2 visits companies that employ PWDs and interview PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and even family members. The video is a part of series of reports that consider how employment should be for PWDs/companies that bring smiles to both parties.
The fifth video introduces Bold, a man with  hearing impairment, who works in the repair department of the Holiday Inn Ulaanbaatar.The Holiday Inn Ulaanbaatar, a five-star hotel that is popular not only as a place for tourists coming to Mongolia from overseas, but also as a venue for various conferences, seminars and events, is also actively engaged in the employment of people with disabilities. Currently, two of the company's 111 employees are a hearing-impaired persons.

DPUB2 visits companies that employ PWDs and interview PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and even family members. The video is a part of series of reports that consider how employment should be for PWDs/companies that bring smiles to both parties.
The forth video introduces Zolbayar, who has a speech impairment caused by cerebral palsy,who  works for Uniservice Solutions LLC(USS). Founded in 1999, USS has worked steadily to promote international standard cleaning services in Mongolia and undertakes cleaning services in Ulaanbaatar, for offices of United Nations agency, embassies of various countries, and the  international airport. Since 2005, the recruitment has gradually expanded its acceptance of persons with disabilities. Now, out of about 900 employees, 29 staff members with hearing impairments and higher brain dysfunctions are working at the head office as cleaners and drivers.

title: Knowledge Forum "How will AI Change Africa?" [JICA]
text:
Knowledge Forum "How will AI Change Africa?" [JICA]
【JICA Ogata Research Institute / United Nations University Knowledge Forum: 
How will AI change Africa?】

Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) technology are expected to bring benefits in various fields ranging from healthcare and education, to economy and governance. However, there are also risks. This includes such problems as AI-generated disinformation, technology and algorithm monopolization by Big Tech, the military use of AI, and intrusive surveillance and misuse of personal data. There are also concerns that AI could widen the existing digital divide between and within countries. Some of these concerns include negative impacts on employment and personal privacy violations when obtaining training data for AI in countries with lax regulations.

In light of the above, the international community is discussing governance frameworks and principles to address the risks brought forth by AI. The UN has played a crucial role in discussions on global AI governance. In a recent landmark initiative, the UN General Assembly adopted the first-ever resolution to respect and protect human rights when using AI. At the G7 Hiroshima Summit, the ”Hiroshima AI Process” was launched under the leadership of the Japanese government, and the OECD has come up with a set of AI principles that have been adopted by member countries as standard. title: Principle of Transit Oriented Development
text:
Principle of Transit Oriented Development
Learning from Cases of ODA Technical Cooperation Project in Urban Transportation and Transit Oriented Development in Dar es Salaam.

Traffic congestion on the main roads of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, has become a problem due to population growth and an increase in the number of private vehicles owned, and the country's government is promoting the development of a Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system as a public transportation system. In order to promote public transportation oriented development (TOD), the key is to identify core stations that will promote TOD and to draw up a TOD strategy for the entire line to guide development toward sustainable growth in Dar es Salaam, where the population is increasing. This project will contribute to the promotion of the TOD approach by developing a TOD strategy and guidelines and a coordination mechanism for relevant agencies along the BRT line in Dar es Salaam, thereby strengthening the capacity of relevant agencies to plan and implement TOD.

This video explains the basic concepts of TOD.

text:

On July 17, 2024, the JICA Ogata Research Institute convened the seminar
“Frontiers of Health Policy and Systems Research (HPSR)”.
2024 will be a pivotal year for Japan to promote health policy and systems
research with global scope, as JICA and Nagasaki University are hosting the 8th
Global Symposium on Health Systems Research (HSR2024) in Nagasaki, Japan, in
cooperation with other collaborators in Japan and the Health Systems Global
(HSG) in November.
The Government of Japan (GoJ) has demonstrated significantleadership role in
setting the global health agendas in recent years through various diplomatic
channels. One of the prominent examples was G7 Hiroshima in 2023 with its
leaders’ communique highlighting their commitment to universal health coverage
(UHC), pandemic prevention, preparedness and response (PPR), and increase
application of innovation, in line with the Japan’s Global Health Strategy
announced in 2022.
Despite Japan’s active political and diplomatic role in influencing and leading
global health agendas, academic and analytical contribution from Japan in global
health has a room to develop, especially in the growing field of health policy
and systems research (HPSR). HPSR with global scope, with particular focus on
the challenges faced by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), is expected to
be further strengthened. This webinar will provide an opportunity to reflect on

title: Book Launch in Manila "Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic" [JICA]
text:
Book Launch in Manila "Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic" [JICA]
The first two years of the COVID-19 pandemic have significantly impeded global development and challenged our understanding of human security. As we tackled various interrelated vulnerabilities, reflecting and reassessing the strategies for ensuring human security became more crucial. 
 In light of the increasing complexity of security challenges we face, the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development has conducted the research project "Human Security and the Practices of Empowerment in East Asia" since 2019, which culminated in the recent publication of a book titled, “Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic.” 

The book is available on the following website: 
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/jica_ri/publication/booksandreports/1521419_24204.html 

On Feb 23, 2024, JICA Ogata Research Institute for Peace and Development and the Department of Political Science of the Ateneo de Manila University co-hosted a book launch seminar to present the key features of the book and discussed lessons from human security issues such as health, gender, aging, and forced displacement intensified by the COVID-19 pandemic.  The seminar included greetings from Dr. Diane Mendoza (Ateneo Political Science Department) and remarks from Prof. Yoichi Mine (JICA Ogata Research Institute). title: ESPD விருதுகள் விழா 2023
text:
ESPD விருதுகள் விழா 2023
2023 நவம்பர் மாதம்இ  திட்ட பங்குதாரர்களால் செய்யப்பட்ட வெற்றிகரமான வேலைவாய்ப்பு நிகழ்வுகளைக் கொண்டாடுவதற்காக இந்த தேசிய மட்டத்திலான விருது வழங்கும் விழா நடாத்தப்பட்டது. ESPD மூலம் வேலை பெற்ற அங்கவீனமுற்ற நபர்கள் மற்றும் அங்கவீனமுற்ற குடும்ப உறுப்பினர்கள்இ அரச உத்தியோகத்தர்கள்இ நிறுவன முகாமையாளர்கள் போன்ற 370 க்கும் மேற்பட்டவர்கள் பங்குபற்றியதுடன் அவர்களுக்கு JICA  ஸ்ரீலங்கா அலுவலகத்தின் தலைமை பிரதிநிதிஇ மகளிர்இசிறுவர் அலுவல்கள் மற்றும் சமூக வலுவுட்டல் அமைச்சின் செயலாளர் மற்றும் சமூக சேவைகள் திணைக்களத்தின் பணிப்பாளர் ஆகியோரின் கைகளால் சான்றிதழ் வழங்கி வைக்கப்பட்டது.
வீடியோவின் இறுதிப் பகுதியில் காட்டப்பட்டுள்ளபடிஇ பங்குதாரர்களின் கருத்துக்கள் ESPD திட்டம் எவ்வாறு அவர்களின் வாழ்க்கையையும் வணிகத்தையும் சாதகமாக வளர்த்துள்ளது என்பதை வெளிப்படுத்துகிறது

2023 නොවැම්බර් මස, මෙම ජාතික මට්ටමේ උත්සවය පවත්වනු ලැබූවේ ව්‍යාපෘතියේ පාර්ශවකරුවන් විසින් ලබාගත් සාර්ථක සිද්ධි අගය කිරීම වෙනුවෙනි. මේ සඳහා ESPD ව්‍යාපෘතිය  අබාධ සහිත පුද්ගලයන් සහ ඔවුන්ගේ පවුල් වල අය, රජයේ නිලධාරීන් , ව්‍යාපාර කලමනාකරුවන්, 370කට අධික පිරිසක් සහභාගී වූ අතර ඔවුන්ට JICA ශ්‍රී ලංකා හි ප්‍රධාන නියෝජිතවරයා, කාන්තා, ළමා කටයුතු සහ සමාජ සවිබලගැන්වීම් අමාත්‍යාංශයේ ලේකම්තුමිය සහ සමාජ සේවා දෙපාර්තමේන්තුවේ අධ්‍යක්ෂකතුමිය අතින් සහතිකපත් ප්‍රධානය කෙරුණි. 
වීඩියෝ පටයේ අවසන් කොටසේ දැක්වෙන ආකාරයට, පාර්ශවකරුවන්ගේ අදහස් මගින් ප්‍රකාශ වන්නේ ESPD වැඩසටහන මගින් ඔවුන්ගේ ජිවිත මෙන්ම ව්‍යාපර ද ධනාත්මක ලෙස සංවර්ධනය වී ඇති ආකාරයයි.

title: Waste Management in Pacific countries（Samoa）～JICA Clean City Initiative(JCCI）～
text:
Waste Management in Pacific countries（Samoa）～JICA Clean City Initiative(JCCI）～
Today, environmental impact is increasing in developing countries due to economic development and urbanization, waste from mass production and consumption, as well as domestic and industrial wastewater causing water and air pollution. 
To efficiently leverage Japan’s experience, examples, and technology to support developing countries, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) works with the Japanese government, international organizations, and many other stakeholders to spearhead broad initiatives. One of these initiatives, JICA Clean City Initiative (JCCI), was launched in 2021.
This video focuses on the "J-PRISM" project, to be implemented in Samoa,a Pacific country, addressing several waste management challenges in small islands. It also collaborates with Caribbean countries facing similar issues.

title: Let's prepare for Childbirth Healthy Mother, Healthy Baby
text:
Let's prepare for Childbirth Healthy Mother, Healthy Baby
Pakistan’s maternal and child health issues,such as malnutrition of mothers,late presentation and late referrals of patients,are tackled every day in Pakistan Institute of Medical Science (PIMS). 
Doctor,nurse and patients will share their experiences and health messages for every pregnant and lactating mothers,their husbands and family members in Pakistan so that Pakistani families and healthcare workers together can make healthier mothers and babies.

title: Save the lives of mothers and children in PIMS
text:
Save the lives of mothers and children in PIMS
Pakistan Institute of Medical Science (PIMS) is a state-of-art government tertiary care facility in capital city of Pakistan. It is the last resort for mothers and children who require advanced medical care from all the provinces. 
To improve maternal and child health in Pakistan, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have been providing grant aid and technical assistance. PIMS Children Hospital (1983), School of Nursing and Medical Technician (1985) and Maternal and Child Health Care (MCH) Centre (1997) were constructed. In 2023, Maternal and Child Health Intensive Care Centre was newly established by Japanese grant, to meet the increasing demand of advanced treatment for high-risk mothers and babies.

title: 【Palau】"Zero Waste Song"　to promote segregation
text:
【Palau】"Zero Waste Song"　to promote segregation
"Zero Waste song” was born from ICETT’s (International Center for Environmental Technology Transfer) Project to promote waste segregation in Palau as a part of JICA Partnership Program.
"Zero Waste Song" was written by a Palauan participant who participated in a training course in Japan and was impressed by Japanese waste management. The song has since been made into CDs and widely heard on Palauan local radio, conveying the importance of waste segregation.
Please enjoy the beautiful melody along with the beautiful images of Palau!

title: ESPD: பைபர் ஆடைகள் நிறுவணத்தில் இணைப்பை ஏற்படுத்தும் நிகழ்சித்திட்டத்துக்ககூடான Success Case
text:
ESPD: பைபர் ஆடைகள் நிறுவணத்தில் இணைப்பை ஏற்படுத்தும் நிகழ்சித்திட்டத்துக்ககூடான Success Case
2021ம் ஆண்டு நொவம்பர் மாதம் முதல் JICA மற்றும் இலங்கை அரசாங்கம் இணைந்து இயலாமை உடைய நபர்களுக்கான தொழில் ஆதரவை மேம்படுத்தும் செயற்றிட்டத்தை மேற்கொண்டுவருகின்றது. இணைப்பை ஏற்படுத்தும் செயற்றிட்டமே ESPD செயற்றிட்டத்தின் அடித்தளமாகும். இது சமூக சேவைகள் திணைக்களத்தின் சமூக சேவைகளுக்கான உத்தியோகத்தர்கள் மற்றும் மனித வலு மற்றும் தொழில் வாய்ப்புகள் திணைக்களத்தின் மனிதவள அபிவிருத்தி உத்தியோகத்தர்களின் ஒன்றிணைந்த செயற்பாடுகளின் ஊடாக இயலாமை உடைய தொழில் தேடுனர்கள் மற்றும் நிறுவணங்களை தொடர்ப்புபடுத்துகிறது.

இக்காணொளியானது வட மேல் மாகாணத்தின் குருநாகல் மாவட்டத்தில் அமைந்துள்ள பைபர் ஆடைகள் எனும் ஆடைத்தொழிற்சாலையில் இணைப்பை ஏற்படுத்தும் செயற்றிட்டத்துக்கு ஊடாக வெற்றிகரமாக தொழில் ஒன்றைப்பெற்றுக்கொண்ட ஒரு Success Case பற்றியதாகும்.

title: ESPD: A success case of Linkage Creation Program at PIPER CLOTHING
text:

JICA and the Sri Lankan government have been jointly implementing the Project for Promoting Employment Support of Persons with Disabilities (ESPD) since November 2021.

This video introduces a LCP success case at PIPER CLOTHING, a garment factory located in Kurunegala of North Western Province.

title: (JICA Indonesia) New Learning Methods for Sustainable Environmental Education in West Kotawaringin
text:
(JICA Indonesia) New Learning Methods for Sustainable Environmental Education in West Kotawaringin
JICA Partnership Program in collaboration with FC Manis (an NGO focused on Environmental Conservation) is promoting environmental education in Borneo’s UNESCO Biosphere Reserve by empowering local schoolteachers to effectively deliver environmental education to students. 

The final symposium, held on March 6, 2024, attended by over 50 students and teacher comes from various Junior High School and Senior High in School in West Kotawaringin, Central Kalimantan. Additionally, representatives from the Education Department, the Environmental Agency, and Tanjung Puting Nature Conservation also participated in this event.

This project period is from December 2021 to March 2024 having prepared a curriculum and textbooks for students and instructional materials for teachers, implemented training of trainer teachers who also conducted mock classes to students, together with implementation framework for dissemination of project activities.

title: Symposium "Exploring the New Dynamics of the  'Global South'"
text:
Symposium "Exploring the New Dynamics of the  'Global South'"
The international community is currently at the crossroads on how to create a world order under the compound crises including post-pandemic, climate change, and the situations in Ukraine and Palestine. In addition, with the growing presence of the "Global South," how will the existing great power-led international order be transformed in the future? Seeking to establish itself as a new superpower, China has strengthened its relations with developing countries in the Indo-Pacific region through political, economic, cultural, and other channels. China’s infrastructure development projects under its "One Belt, One Road" initiative often take different approaches from those of the Western countries and Japan, and have drawn criticism for their lack of consideration for environmental and human rights issues, and for burdening recipient countries with excessive debts. It has also been said that project recipients are mostly smaller states, making it difficult for them to take the initiative in negotiations with China.

The JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute) has questioned such a big-power-centered explanation, and has conducted research to redefine bilateral relations with China from the perspective of smaller states. title: Knowledge Forum with Prof.Stiglitz "The Future of Employment in a Changing Global Economy"[JICA]
text:
Knowledge Forum with Prof.Stiglitz "The Future of Employment in a Changing Global Economy"[JICA]
There is growing concern around global employment trends. Population growth will increase labor force supply but whether the job creation that meets this will actually follow needs to be closely watched. In particular, in Africa, an exponential growth in the labor force is forecast. According to a medium-range projection by the United Nations, the global increase in the working age population is expected to be around 1.5 billion between 2010 and 2050, of which 1 billion is expected to take place in Africa. The key challenge here is whether inclusive growth that absorbs this increase in the labor force can be realized. Moreover, how employment around the world will be affected by other factors such as advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, changes in economic structure and supply chains following the COVID-19 pandemic, and the transition to a green economy, is yet to be fully understood.

This forum was hosted by the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute), together with the Initiative for Policy Dialogue (IPD), a non-profit research initiative at Columbia University, and discussed these issues around employment from multiple angles, spanning both macro and micro perspectives.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 3 Jur Ur Bakery, Mongolia
text:
Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 3 Jur Ur Bakery, Mongolia
In Mongolia, legal systems are being developed to guarantee the rights of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and promote their social participation. What changes will be made to PWDs and companies when working in companies? What considerations are required?

DPUB2 visits companies that employ PWDs and interview PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and even family members. The video is a part of series of reports that consider how employment should be for PWDs/companies that bring smiles to both parties.

The third video introduced Odgerel , a woman of dwarfism, works at Jur Ur, a bakery stores company. The company’s mission is to “Share Happiness (deliver and share happiness with people)”, and expanding its business widely in Mongolia. Since 2007, the company has actively promoted the employment of persons with hearing, visual, and physical impairments, currently, out of about 1,000 employees, more than 35 persons with disabilities are engaged in cleaning, sales, office work, packaging, manufacturing, and other operations.

title: Seminar“Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic"[JICA］
text:
Seminar“Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic"[JICA］
The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic has significantly contributed to a considerable setback in global development and has highlighted the unprecedented challenges it presented to human security. Given the growing complexity of human security threats, the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development has conducted the research project "Human Security and the Practices of Empowerment in East Asia" since 2019, which culminated in the recent publication of a book titled, “Human Security and Empowerment in Asia: Beyond the Pandemic.”

The book is available in the following website.
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/jica_ri/publication/booksandreports/1521419_24204.html

On Nov. 30, 2023, the JICA Ogata Research Institute, in cooperation with Sophia University, convened a book launch seminar at Sophia University in Tokyo to share findings of the research project that focuses on the unique empowerment narratives of specific vulnerable populations within the Southeast Asian region and Japan. Following welcome remarks by Chie Miyahara, director general of the JICA Ogata Research Institute, and Ken Aoki, director of the Sophia Institute for Human Security, three editors discussed how lessons learned so far could help us move towards human security.

text:
Proyecto DRIP de Paz en Génova,Colombia(Full_Esp)
Tras más de medio siglo de conflicto armado, Colombia firmó en 2016 un histórico acuerdo de paz entre el Gobierno y las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias para evitar la reaparición del conflicto.El proyecto de cooperación técnica de JICA (DRIP de PAZ) se posiciona como el primer pilar del acuerdo de paz “Reforma Rural Integral” y pretende contribuir a la realización de la paz en el país reduciendo la disparidad económica entre las zonas urbanas y rurales, considerada una de las principales causas del conflicto.

title: Seminar "Industry Engagement in TVET: Experiences from East Asia" 【JICA/AUDA-NEPAD Joint Webinar】
text:
Seminar "Industry Engagement in TVET: Experiences from East Asia" 【JICA/AUDA-NEPAD Joint Webinar】
The JICA Ogata Research Institute and AUDA-NEPAD Policy Bridge Tank jointly hosted a webinar, with a focus on the development of industrial human resources (HRD). 

The development of human resources that aligns with labor market demands is a crucial priority for many countries, particularly in Africa where addressing youth employment is high on the agenda. Japan has a wealth of experience in supporting industrial HRD in developing countries, which includes the capacity development of TVET institutions for industry linkages.

In this context, the JICA Ogata Research Institute shared two East Asian examples based on its research findings: (i) promoting industry engagement in Vietnam; and (ii) learning and localizing industrial technologies in Thailand. 

The experiences from East Asia will provide valuable insights and contribute to the co-creation of practical knowledge for industrial development in Africa.

title: 【Côte d'Ivoire】2023 Africa Cup of Nations (AfCON) ZERO WASTE ～JICA Advocacy Project～
text:
【Côte d'Ivoire】2023 Africa Cup of Nations (AfCON) ZERO WASTE ～JICA Advocacy Project～
Have you ever heard of the AfCON? The AfCON stands for "African Cup of Nations", which is the biggest football tournament bringing together the best African nations and the biggest sporting event on the continent. Held every two years, it is as exciting and festive for all Africans as the World Cup. And this year, the 2023 edition will be played in Côte d'Ivoire!

Many of you may remember that during the 2022 World Cup, Japanese fans collected rubbish in the stadium after their team's match. Inspired by this fine example, the Ivorian authorities and JICA Côte d'Ivoire have agreed to promote an initiative called the "AfCON ZERO WASTE" campaign during this AfCON 2023 and thus share this Japanese spirit of discipline and cleanliness.

This collaboration has involved support in the form of cleanliness kits, training and the production of an awareness-raising video. This video will also provide a link with our waste management projects in Côte d'Ivoire, in which we promote the Reduction, Reuse and Recycling (3R) of waste.
Watch it and together enjoy a clean AfCON, a ZERO WASTE AfCON!

title: Knowledge Forum "Making Japan the Chosen Country" [JICA]
text:
Knowledge Forum "Making Japan the Chosen Country" [JICA]
In Japan, labor shortages are becoming more serious due to the declining birthrate and aging population, as well as a shrinking workforce, and efforts to accept migrant workers from abroad are expanding. The number of migrant workers has increased significantly over the past decade from 650,000 in 2011 to 1,724,000 in 2020 — a 2.7-fold increase — and their share of the workforce has increased from 1.0% to 2.6%. A study by the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute) predicts a demand of 3.56 million workers in 2030 and 6.32 million workers in 2040. While the number of international migrant workers is on the rise, with migrant workers from Asian countries amounting to approximately six million every year, Japan has a lot to do to be selected as a destination country. This includes addressing problems such as human rights violations of technical interns, and the immobilization of precarious workers including fake foreign students establishing a safe and secure work environment for foreign workers without mismatches or high fees, and drawing up future-oriented initiatives to make Japan more attractive in comparison to other receiving countries. In addition, bilateral collaboration will be key to establishing these safe and attractive migration routes, taking into account the mechanisms for selecting international migration routes not only in the country receiving workers, Japan, but also in the countries sending them.

The Project was implemented in the five northern regions of Ghana over a period of six years, from 2017 to 2023.
The Project aimed to strengthen community health services by utilizing the Life-course Approach. title: Knowledge Forum "How Can Japan Contribute to Quality Infrastructure Investment?"[JICA]
text:
Knowledge Forum "How Can Japan Contribute to Quality Infrastructure Investment?"[JICA]
Knowledge Forum "How Can Japan Contribute to Quality Infrastructure Investment in Developing Countries? Learning from Cases of ODA in Urban Transportation"[JICA]

Infrastructure investment in developing countries faces not only challenges in financial resource mobilization but also in quality improvement. In recent years, Japan has been advocating the importance of quality infrastructure investment to the global community and the G20 Principles for Quality Infrastructure Investment were endorsed at the G20 Osaka Summit in 2019. These principles emphasize the importance of the following: maximizing the positive impacts of infrastructure; economic efficiency in light of life-cycle cost; environmental consideration and resilience; inclusiveness; and infrastructure governance (such as ensuring transparency and debt sustainability).

This symposium covered one of the most well-known fields where Japan is actively contributing to quality infrastructure investment, which is the development of urban transportation infrastructure such as metro systems. By leveraging the knowledge and experience gained through development and operation of urban transportation within Japan over the years, Japan has provided a lot of assistance in this field, mainly in Southeast and South Asia. The outcomes of such cooperation, along with the collaboration with stakeholders in developing countries, were presented in the symposium. There also were reports on activities around transit-oriented development,

title: JICA’s Assistance to Upgrade Girls’ Schools in Sindh Province, Pakistan (Long ver.)
text:
JICA’s Assistance to Upgrade Girls’ Schools in Sindh Province, Pakistan (Long ver.)
Education is a basic human right and the foundation of nation building.

In rural Sindh, only 20% of girls enrol at middle level, as compared to 47% of boys.
In urban areas, that rate increases to 66% for girls and 72% for boys.

Girls who complete secondary school education are better able to participate in economic and social activities and raise healthier and better educated children. 
They contribute to more stable societies, which give all individuals the opportunity to better fulfil their potential. 

In this context, the Sindh Government is making efforts to improve access to quality education, especially for girls.

JICA has been supporting the effort of the Sindh Government by upgrading 54 girls' primary schools into elementary schools in Rural Sindh. 

These schools were designed and built taking into account the damages caused by the 2010 flood. As a result, they sustained the 2022 floods without significant damages and many of them were used as shelters for Internally Displaced Persons.

 “Building Back Better (BBB)” is the key approach to post-disaster recovery to reduce vulnerability to future disasters and establish the environment that supports children's continuous learning.

title: Knowledge Forum "Energy Crisis and Climate Change"[JICA]
text:
Knowledge Forum "Energy Crisis and Climate Change"[JICA]
The international energy situation has become unstable due to a combination of various factors, including increased demand from the resumption of economic activities following the COVID-19 pandemic, supply constraints resulting from reduced investment in fossil fuels, and Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Energy prices have been on a downward trend since their sharp rise in 2022; however, there still remains a risk of further price hikes and disruptions in the market. Higher energy prices could lead to higher costs for a variety of economic activities. This energy crisis became an opportunity to realize and reaffirm the importance of energy security.

At this Knowledge Forum, Professor Kikkawa Takeo of the International University of Japan, expert in energy, provided a keynote speech. Ms. Morishita Maiko from the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies (IGES) and the Climate Bonds Initiative, as well as JICA Ogata Research Institute Executive Senior Research Fellow Sato Ichiro, joined the discussion with Professor Kikkawa on energy security and climate change.

title: Seminar “Adaptive Peacebuilding: A New Approach to Sustaining Peace in the 21st Century”[JICA]
text:
Seminar “Adaptive Peacebuilding: A New Approach to Sustaining Peace in the 21st Century”[JICA]
This seminar introduced the edited volume, “Adaptive Peacebuilding: A New Approach to Sustaining Peace in the 21st Century,” which aims to address the changing landscape of conflict and develop new and complementary approaches to sustaining peace. The editors, Prof. Cedric de Coning (Research Professor, Research Group on Peace, Conflict, and Development, Norwegian Institute of International Affairs), Dr. Rui Saraiva (Lecturer, Miyazaki International University), Dr. Ako Muto (Specially Appointed Research Fellow, JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development) introduced the concept of “adaptive peacebuilding” and discussed how it was tested through eight case studies across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America. They presented the cases of Syria and Mozambique, which showcase geographical diversity, and provide different types of conflict and a wide range of actors within the broader peace field.

This book is an outcome of the research project titled "Contextualizing International Cooperation for Sustaining Peace: Adaptive Peacebuilding Pathways.”

text:

DPUB2 visits companies that employ PWDs and interview PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and even family members. The video is a part of series of reports that consider how employment should be for PWDs/companies that bring smiles to both parties.

title: Promotion of Social Participation of Persons with Disabilities through Sports(Digest)
text:
Promotion of Social Participation of Persons with Disabilities through Sports(Digest)
JICA promotes the realization of a peaceful society where all people can equally choose to enjoy sport regardless of gender, age, culture, social or economic status, or disability. Aiming to promote social participation of persons with disabilities through sports, JICA has been conducting "Knowledge Co-Creation Program: Promotion of Social Participation of Persons with Disabilities through Sports" for many years by inviting participants from a wide range of regions in Asia, Africa, and Oceania to Japan.
In many cases, there are inadequate facilities, equipment, and environments for persons with disabilities to participate in sports, and funds for improvements are lacking.In light of these issues, JICA provides a variety of knowledge and skills, from understanding the social model of disability to the rules, teaching methods, and awareness-raising for inclusive sports.
What challenges exist in the social participation of persons with disabilities and how JICA aims to solve those challenges through sports will be explained,including the acchievements of the training participants.

The World Bank Group and the JICA Ogata Research Institute hosted a seminar " Progress of the World Bank Group’s Fragility, Conflict, Violence Strategy and Collaboration with JICA " on February 21, 2023. title: Cooperación Regional SICA-JICA (2021-2025)
text:
Cooperación Regional SICA-JICA (2021-2025)
【English】
The Central American Integration System (SICA) is the institutional framework of regional cooperation, composed of eight States of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Belize, and the Dominican Republic, promoting regional integration mainly in the following five areas: Democratic security, Climate change and Comprehensive risk management, Social integration, Economic integration, and Institutional strengthening. This video was produced to introduce the efforts and achievements related to the SICA-JICA Regional Cooperation Action Plan (2021-2025), which was agreed upon between SICA and JICA.

El Sistema de la Integración Centroamericana (SICA) es el marco institucional de la integración regional, compuesto por los Estados de Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panamá, Belice y la República Dominicana, promoviendo la integración regional principalmente en los siguientes pilares: seguridad democrática, cambio climático y gestión integral del riesgo, integración social, integración económica, y fortalecimiento institucional. JICA promueve la cooperación regional en diversos campos enviando expertos al SICA desde el año 2000.

title: Rebuilding Resilient Nepal
text:
Rebuilding Resilient Nepal
On 25 April 2015, a devastating earthquake of magnitude 7.8 struck Nepal with its epicentre in the Gorkha district. The earthquake caused widespread destruction and tremendous impacts on various aspects of the Nepalese society. Iimmediately after the earthquake, the Government of Japan provided emergency response and JICA has been providing assistance to the Government of Nepal (GoN) in reconstruction and recovery based on the principle of Build Back Better (BBB). JICA’s BBB-based reconstruction and recovery support has covered various sectors, such as housing and school reconstruction, cultural heritage, infrastructure reconstruction, livelihood recovery and so on.

JICA’s assistance for reconstruction and recovery has almost come to an end, and the focus of JICA’s assistance has shifted to long-term capacity building to contribute to future disaster risk reduction, drawing on the lessons learned from this reconstruction and recovery assistance. This video aims to showcase the various efforts and achievements that have taken place in the last eight years since earthquake, highlighting how JICA’s assistance has contributed to realize BBB and further to support strengthening of resilience in Nepal.

title: [JICA INDONESIA] User Training for Vaccine Icelined Refrigerators in Indonesia February 2023 (Short)
text:
[JICA INDONESIA] User Training for Vaccine Icelined Refrigerators in Indonesia February 2023 (Short)
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in collaboration with Bengkulu Provincial Health Office organized the one-day user training on the operation and maintenance of the Vaccine Icelined Refrigerator on 9 February 2023 at Bengkulu City, Bengkulu Province in Indonesia. 
The training was implemented under the JICA’s technical cooperation for “The Project for Strengthening Capacity Building Management of Vaccination and Laboratory for COVID-19 and Other Infectious Diseases".

There were a total of 21 participants, vaccine and cold chain store managers and technicians, from Bengkulu Province, who participated in the training. The training was held in association with the above JICA project to donate 330 units of Vestfrost-made Vaccine Icelined refrigerators (VLS404A) to Indonesia. This user training was composed of lectures and theories and practical “hands-on” sessions to train Cold Chain users to brush up their knowledge and skills on proper maintenance of the equipment and accessories to be supplied by JICA. 

Through this training, we brief this technical support to the Ministry of Health, the Republic of Indonesia officials, and other provincial health office people to urge other target provinces to follow. JICA hope this activity could be widely watched by JICA people and other Japanese who are involved with international cooperation.

【JICA TANZANIA】Changing Farmers’ Mind Set from “Grow and Sell' to ‘Grow to Sell' (TANSHEP) Short ver
Agriculture in Tanzania is an important sector, with about 65% of the population engaged in agriculture and accounting for about 25% of GDP. However, its productivity and profitability were low, and shifting to higher value-added agriculture has been one of the major challenges. One of the reasons for low profitability is that farmers grow and sell crops without knowing the market needs. Therefore, we have been promoting the "SHEP (Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion)" , an approach that changes the mindset of farmers from "grow and sell" to "grow to sell," and trying to improve the farming and cultivation skills of horticultural farmers. This video provides an overview of the "SHEP" approach practice in Tanzania and shows success attained by farmers who practice it.

title: Projet « École pour Tous » en Afrique（court）
text:
Projet « École pour Tous » en Afrique（court）
Projet « École pour Tous » en Afrique : Les données montrent une amélioration spectaculaire de l'éducation des enfants
Les parents du monde entier souhaitent offrir à leurs enfants une éducation de qualité. 
Cependant, en Afrique subsaharienne, par exemple, près de 90 % des enfants d'âge scolaire primaire ne parviennent pas à atteindre les niveaux de compétence minimum en lecture et en mathématiques. 
De plus, la pandémie de COVID-19 a exacerbé la « crise de l'apprentissage » en nécessitant des mesures telles que la fermeture des écoles.
Dans ce contexte, le projet « École pour Tous » de la JICA a considérablement amélioré les compétences académiques de base des enfants africains en améliorant l'environnement d'apprentissage en collaboration avec les écoles, les parents et les communautés locales. 
Le projet, qui a commencé en 2004 dans 23 écoles primaires au Niger, s'est maintenant étendu à environ 70 000 écoles primaires et secondaires dans neuf pays africains, et ses réalisations ont attiré l'attention du monde entier.

Plus de détails peuvent être trouvés dans cet article.
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/field/2022/20221118_11.html

title: Supporting Ukraine with made-in-Japan landmine detection technology（Short）
text:
Supporting Ukraine with made-in-Japan landmine detection technology（Short）
Japanese Technology to Support Demining Efforts in Ukraine! Training on made-in-Japan landmine detection in Cambodia

In January 2023, the Japanese government, through JICA, invited expert officials from the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) to Cambodia for training on the latest Japanese landmine detectors.

Due to Russian invasion, as much as 30% of the land in Ukraine could be contaminated with hazardous explosive remnants of war, such as landmines and unexploded ordnance. It is estimated that it will take at least 10 years. 

JICA's project aims to remove these explosives in Ukraine as quickly and safely as possible in anticipation of postwar reconstruction.

title: School for All Project（Short）
text:
School for All Project（Short）
School for All Project in Africa: Data shows dramatic improvement in children’s education

Parents around the globe want to provide their children with a quality education. 
In Sub-Saharan Africa, for example, almost 90 percent of primary-school-aged children are not achieving the minimum proficiency levels in reading and mathematics. 
Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated the “learning crisis” by necessitating such measures as school closures.

Against such a backdrop, the JICA “School for All” project has dramatically improved the basic academic skills of African children by improving the learning environment for children in collaboration with schools, parents, and local communities. 
The project, which started in 2004 at 23 primary schools in Niger, has now spread to about 70,000 primary and secondary schools in nine African countries, and its achievements have attracted worldwide attention.

More details can be found in this article.
https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/field/2022/20221118_11.html

Depuis 2019, le bureau de l’Agence Japonaise de Coopération Internationale (JICA) au Burkina Faso accompagne le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des Langues Nationales (MENAPLN) dans la promotion de l’approche « Etude de Leçon ». D’origine japonaise et adaptée au contexte burkinabè par des anciens stagiaires burkinabè et volontaires japonais, cette approche est un outil efficace d’autoformation permettant aux enseignants de réfléchir sur leurs propres pratiques pédagogiques afin de les améliorer et faciliter ainsi les apprentissages des élèves.

title: BACK FROM THE RUBBLES-JICA’s cooperation in Nepal-
text:
BACK FROM THE RUBBLES-JICA’s cooperation in Nepal-
The Gorkha Earthquake in 2015 caused severe loss and damage to heritage monuments in Nepal. JICA dispatched “Cultural Heritage Advisor” to support The Department of Archaeology (DoA) on heritage conservation and to provide technical advice. In Japan, the main concept of the heritage buildings reconstruction is to preserve the authenticity of the building. The Expert, Dr. Toshimichi Okumura has been working for 4 years in Nepal and organized workshops and seminars about cultural heritage buildings rehabilitation for DoA staff and Colleges students. He and DoA are now working on rehabilitation of Shiva Temple with original structure, and using original materials as much as possible as a model of preserving the authenticity.

title: Formation sur la technologie Do-Nou avec la JICA Burkina Faso
text:
Formation sur la technologie Do-Nou avec la JICA Burkina Faso
Le Burkina Faso est un pays enclavé et sans accès à la mer, la route joue donc un rôle très important dans son développement. Le bureau local de la JICA a offert aux acteurs en charge de l’entretien des routes en terre du pays une formation sur la technologie DO-NOU. Cette technologie développée au Japon est mise en œuvre dans plus de 25 pays en Afrique. 
Grâce à son faible coût et à l’utilisation des matériaux locaux, elle pourrait contribuer à l’entretien de routes en terre aussi bien dans les zones urbaines que rurales. Elle peut aussi être utilisée pour construire des infrastructures de protection tel que des digues, des retenues d’eaux ou des ouvrages de franchissement.

title: Хөдөлмөр эрхлэхийг хүссэн хүн бүрд ээлтэй нийгмийг хамтдаа бүтээцгээе”
text:
Хөдөлмөр эрхлэхийг хүссэн хүн бүрд ээлтэй нийгмийг хамтдаа бүтээцгээе”
Монгол улсын ХНХЯ болон Жайка ОУБ-аас хэрэгжүүлж буй техникийн хамтын ажиллагааны “Хөгжлийн бэрхшээлтэй иргэдийн хөдөлмөр эрхлэлтийг дэмжих тогтолцоог бэхжүүлэх төсөл DPUB2” нь, хөдөлмөр эрхлэх хүсэл эрмэлзэлтэй хөгжлийн бэрхшээлтэй иргэн болон аж ахуй нэгж байгууллагыг хооронд холбох “Ажлын байрны дадлагажуулагч ” гэсэн мэргэшсэн хүний нөөцийг бэлтгэн, ажлын үнэлгээ хийхээс эхлээд ажилд томилох, ажилд сургах, бие даан ажиллах хүртэлх цогц дэмжлэгийг үзүүлэх “Ажлын байрны дадлагажуулагчийн ажлын байранд дэмжлэг үзүүлэх үйлчилгээ”-г хүргэх ажлыг зохион байгуулж байна. 
 Энэхүү шинэ тогтолцооны талаар та бүхэнд танилцуулах үүднээс DPUB2 төслөөс нөлөөллийн видеог бэлтгэсэн юм. 2021 оны намраас өвлийг дамжин Токио, Улаанбаатар хотуудад зураг авалт хийж, Токио хотод эвлүүлгийг нь хийсэн 1 минутын энэхүү видеонд дэлгэцийг хоёр хэсэгт хуваан, монголд ажиллаж буй хөгжлийн бэрхшээлтэй ажилтанд япон ажлын байрны дадлагажуулагч зөвлөгөө өгч дадлагажуулж буй байдлыг ойлгомжтойгоор хүргэхийн зэрэгцээ, монгол ажилтнууд инээмсэглэл тодруулан ажиллаж байгааг харуулсан сэтгэл хоногшихуйц видео болсон гэж бодож байна.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
text:
Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
Mongolia Job Coach employment support service awareness-raising video 

　The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection in Mongolia and the JICA technical cooperation Project for Promoting Employment of Persons with Disabilities in Mongolia (DPUB2) train specialist personnel called 'job coach' to match people with disabilities who wish to work with companies. The project is promoting the provision of a 'job coach employment support service' that provides consistent support from job assessment to assignment, adaptation to the workplace and retention.
　To inform people about this new system, which has never existed in Mongolia before, DPUB2 has produced an awareness-raising video, shot in Tokyo and Ulaanbaatar during the autumn and winter of 2021, and edited in Tokyo, the one-minute video splits the screen into two halves, showing persons with disabilities working in Mongolia and a Japanese support. The video is warm and impressive, and symbolically expressing the smiles that are spreading across Mongolia.

JICA marks its 60th anniversary of its cooperation activities with Tanzania in 2022. The activities began in 1962, just one year after the independence of Tanganyika, when a single Government Official was accepted for technical training in Japan. 
Since then, the activities of JICA continued to grow over the years and now include not only technical cooperation and Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV), but also the provision of grant aid and concessionary loans. Over the 60 years, JICA’s activities have continued to grow and expand to support many social and economic development activities.JICA will carry out its activities in line with Tanzania's development plan.

title: IUJ-JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum
text:
IUJ-JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum
Amidst the extensive socioeconomic and political consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic still in effect, the Russian invasion of Ukraine broke out this February. This has created a crisis on top of another crisis, or compounded crises that have put the world into an extremely precarious situation. For example, stagnation of exportation from Russia and Ukraine following the invasion is causing a global supply shortage of food and energy, which is greatly impacting people’s livelihoods in the world. Furthermore, in addition to price surges, significant currency depreciations and worsening national debt situations, the global macroeconomic outlook is worsening as well, as seen in the deceleration of economic growth in China. 
IUJ-JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum ‘Security and Development Cooperation in Compounded Crises: the Impacts of the Ukraine Crisis, and State, Economic, and Human Security’ was held on December 16, 2022. The session identified various global challenges under today’s compounded crises from the perspectives of state security, economic security, and human security and then discussed measures to enhance resilience and stability.

title: JICA Volunteers in Saint Lucia - Shiatsu Massage
text:
JICA Volunteers in Saint Lucia - Shiatsu Massage
JICA presents, its Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV) program in Saint Lucia.

In this series of videos called JICA Volunteers in Saint Lucia, we take a look at the highlights of volunteers` contribution to the socio-development of Saint Lucia. 

Second,we present Mr. Akira TSUNAKAWA. 

As part of a revenue generating initiative by the Saint Lucia Blind Welfare Association (SLBWA), Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteer (JOCV), Mr. Akira Tsunakawa is teaching shiatsu, (a Japanese massage technique) to blind and visually impaired students. Mr. Tsunakawa, who is totally blind, is a teacher of oriental medicine and has worked with the Yokohama School for the Blind for over 25 years. He is now sharing his vast experience and expertise in shiatsu techniques from his hands to those of his students.

His intentions are to provide the students with shiatsu training to become professional shiatsu therapists. The classes are four times a week from Monday to Thursday and will last for one year. Students are also learning anatomy and physiology as part of the training. The class includes five blind and partially sighted students who have had to wait approximately two years for this valuable opportunity due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
text:
Good Practice of Employing Persons with Disabilities, Case 1, APU Company, Mongolia
In Mongolia, legal systems are being developed to guarantee the rights of persons with disabilities (PWDs) and promote their participation in society.What changes will be made to both PWDs and companies when they work in companies? And what considerations are required to further promote the employment of PWDs?
 The Mongolian Ministry of Labour and Social Security and JICA are implementing the Project for Promoting Employment of Persons with Disabilities (DPUB2), in which they are visiting companies that employ PWDs and interviewing PWDs, company personnel, colleagues and sometimes even family members. The articles are part of a series of articles that consider how employment should be for PWDs and companies that bring smiles to the faces of both parties.
 The first video is from the APU Company, the largest beverage manufacturer in Mongolia. Ts. Zhavzmaa, who has a congenital hearing loss and speech impediment, used to lose her confidence because people always pointed out what she couldn't do, such as "I can't hear" or "I can't speak well". However, this has changed dramatically since she started working at the APU Company warehouse a year ago.

title: OGATA Sadako Symposium, "What Would You Do?"
text:
OGATA Sadako Symposium, "What Would You Do?"
▼ OGATA Sadako Symposium, "What Would You Do?"  ▼

ーWhat we can learn from Ms. OGATA Sadako and how we should live our livesー 


This month marks 3 years since OGATA Sadako, who served as UN High Commissioner for Refugees and President of Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), passed away in October 2019. The world has changed dramatically in just 3 years.


"What would you do?" If Ms. Ogata were alive, she might say this.


On November 15, 2022, JICA held a symposium to discuss the future of the world and Japan by reflecting on OGATA's life and achievements.


Approximately 4,200 people attended the symposium, and we hope that the audience was able to learn Ms. OGATA's way of life and way of thinking, and that it provided an opportunity for each of us, who have been entrusted with her baton, to think about how we should live our lives.

title: JICA Cold Chain Equipment Maintenance Training for West Kalimantan and West Java in Oct 2022 (Full)
text:
JICA Cold Chain Equipment Maintenance Training for West Kalimantan and West Java in Oct 2022 (Full)
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in collaboration with West Java Provincial Health Office organized the 2 days training of the maintenance of Cold Chain equipment on 26 and 27 October at Bandung, West Java. The training was implemented under the JICA’s technical cooperation for “The Project for Strengthening Capacity Building Management of Vaccination and Laboratory for COVID-19 and Other Infectious Disease".

There were total of 13 participants, vaccine and cold chain technicians, from 7 areas of West Kalimantan and West Java, participated in the training. The training was composed with lectures and theories and practical “hand-on” sessions to train trainers to brush up their knowledge and skills on proper maintenance of the equipment and accessories to be supplied by JICA. 

Through this training, we brief this technical support to the central Ministry of Health officials and other provincial health office people to urge other target provinces to follow. JICA hope this activity could be widely watched by JICA people and other Japanese who are involved with international cooperation. JICA appreciates all participants for their active participation for the training!

text:
JICA Indonesia organized 2 days maintenance training on Cold Chain equipment in Sept 2022 (Full)

title: JICA Indonesia organized 2 days maintenance training on respiratory equipment in August 2022 (Short)
text:
JICA Indonesia organized 2 days maintenance training on respiratory equipment in August 2022 (Short)
Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in collaboration with West Java Provincial Health Office, Indonesia, organized 2 days equipment maintenance training on 23rd and 24th August 2022 after the donation of the 400 units of Oxygen concentrators to Indonesia in November 2021. 
This 2 days training was composed with lecture, theories and practical “hand-on” sessions to train trainers to ensure appropriate operation and maintenance of the donated equipment.
There were total of 19 participants, users and equipment technicians, from 7 health facilities participated in the training. The training participants are expected to organize the domestic trainings to train their staff and colleagues at their workplaces on what they learnt from this training as trainers.   
We created this PR video to brief this technical support to the central Ministry of Health officials and other provincial health office people to urge other target provinces to follow.
We are also grateful for the video to be widely watched by JICA people and other Japanese who are involved with international cooperation.
JICA will continue to support the Indonesia Ministry of Health’s efforts to fight against COVID-19 control and treatment.

title: Floricultura Argentina(avance)
text:
Floricultura Argentina(avance)
En la historia de la inmigración japonesa a la Argentina es ampliamente conocido, que muchos de los inmigrantes japoneses se dedicaron a la floricultura. 
　En la década del '70 JICA estableció el Centro Tecnológico de Flori-Fruti-Horticultura (conocido como CETTEFHO) como parte de su apoyo a los inmigrantes. Más tarde, con la plena integración de la comunidad de japoneses y sus descendientes, el centro tecnológico modificó sus funciones y fue transferido al Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) en 2004, donde renació como el actual Instituto de Floricultura.
　El Instituto de Floricultura del INTA se ha desarrollado hasta convertirse en un líder de la investigación florícola no sólo en el país sino también en la región. En la actualidad, el sistema de investigación se ha ampliado enormemente, se han introducido diversas variedades nuevas mediante la mejora y el desarrollo, y se ha establecido una red en torno al instituto para proporcionar orientación técnica a los floricultures de todo el país. Además, en los últimos años, en colaboración con empresas japonesas, el instituto ha establecido un sistema por el cual los beneficios o regalías se distribuyen también a los lugares de recolección de recursos genéticos utilizados en el desarrollo de nuevas variedades.
  JICA en conjunto con el gobierno argentino, impulsa la cooperación triangular con el INTA y en los últimos 10 años ha implementado el programa de capacitación para terceros países en la región de  Améric

title: Startups in Africa – the grand final of the NINJA accelerator program competition in Nigeria
text:
Startups in Africa – the grand final of the NINJA accelerator program competition in Nigeria
Nikkei and JICA (Japan International Cooperation Agency) hosted a pitch event focusing on new technology businesses in Nigeria and broadcasted the live Zoom webinar in English and Japanese (simultaneous translation). Six entrepreneurs selected from the NINJA accelerator program made pitch presentations and appealed their new tech businesses in front of thousands of web audiences. We believe this pitch event became a milestone strengthening business ties between Japan and African countries.

At the event, several Japanese specialists had also keynote speeches and panel discussion to talk about the potential Japan-Africa partnership and to encourage more investments in African startups.

*Project NINJA=Next INnovation with Japan
