title: Project History Launch “Japan-Thailand Environmental Cooperation -35 Years of People-to-People Ties”
text:
Project History Launch “Japan-Thailand Environmental Cooperation -35 Years of People-to-People Ties”
JICA Ogata Research Institute has published the "Project History" book series, which looks back on JICA's projects, analyzing and summarizing their trajectories and achievements. As the 29th volume in this series, "Japan-Thailand Environmental Cooperation: 35 Years of People-to-People Ties" has been published. 

This book introduces the history of Japan-Thailand environmental cooperation, focusing on people-to-people ties and summarizing the growth of both the Japanese and Thai parties involved. Fukuda, Seki and Watanabe, three former JICA experts who wrote the book, emphasize that "it is the relationship of trust between people that determines the success or failure of a project. The humanistic activities of these "old generation experts," who do not fit into the framework of project evaluation, provide us with a great deal of insight into the nature of development cooperation.

On May 31, 2022, a seminar was held to commemorate the publication of the book. After an introduction of the book by a representative of the book's author group, a panel discussion by various stakeholders and a roundtable discussion with young experts was held on the theme of building, maintaining, and passing on trust in international cooperation.

title: Side Event COSP-15 The Revolution of Independent Living in Latin America
text:
Side Event COSP-15 The Revolution of Independent Living in Latin America
Side Event｜15th Session of the Conference of States Parties to the CRPD 15 June 2022 (18:00-19:15) Independent Living Revolution in Latin America: Persons with Disabilities as Protagonists of International Cooperation

The session explores how the independent living movement has been advancing in Latin America with the initiative of persons with disabilities, supported by their peers within the region and beyond. It looks at how international cooperation has facilitated an awareness of persons with disabilities of their right to independent living, the establishment of the first independent living center in Costa Rica, and the creation of the Latin American Network for Independent Living (RELAVIN).
The discussion focuses on the experiences of the RELAVIN members at different stages of their journey on independent living. It ensures the effectiveness of international cooperation delivered by organizations of persons with disabilities and the critical role of development agencies. The session makes a call to action to all stakeholders including organizations of persons with disabilities to collaborate for the development of policies and systems for independent living.

title: Evento Paralelo COSP-15 Revolución de la Vida Independiente en Latino América
text:
Evento Paralelo COSP-15 Revolución de la Vida Independiente en Latino América
Evento paralelo de la 15°Conferencia de los Estados Partes en la Convención sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad “Revolución de la Vida Independiente en Latino América: Personas con Discapacidad como Protagonistas de la Cooperación Internacional” 
 
La sesión explorará cómo el movimiento de vida independiente ha ido avanzando en América Latina con la iniciativa de las personas con discapacidad, apoyadas por sus pares dentro y de japón. Se analizará cómo la cooperación internacional ha facilitado la concienciación de las personas con discapacidad sobre su derecho a la vida independiente, el establecimiento del primer centro de vida independiente en Costa Rica y la creación de la Red Latinoamericana de Vida Independiente (RELAVIN).

El diálogo se centra en las experiencias de los miembros de RELAVIN en las diferentes etapas de su camino hacia la vida independiente. Al compartir sus experiencias, la sesión pretende demostrar cómo la cooperación internacional puede facilitar el movimiento de la vida independiente y hace un llamamiento a la acción a todas las partes interesadas, incluidas las organizaciones de personas con discapacidad, para que colaboren en el desarrollo de políticas y sistemas de vida independiente 
 
Organizadores: JICA, Red Latinoamericana de Vida Independiente (RELAVIN), Asociación Mainstream

title: Responsive learning initiative taken for Out-of-School Children in Pakistan
text:
Responsive learning initiative taken for Out-of-School Children in Pakistan
There are 22.8 million out-of-school children and youth (OOSC) in Pakistan. Out of the number, 78% are overage, in other words, missed chance to enroll formal education system at appropriate age. 

Hassnain, 12 years boy who had never been to school and working in a riksha workshop in Multan, South Punjab, was one of them. 

The Advancing Quality Alternative Learning Project (AQAL) Phase 2 is working with the Government of Pakistan to provide quality responsive education through Accelerated Learning Program (ALP) for OOSC. Morning school for working children in which Hassnain studies, is one of the ALP school established by the government. Upon completion of the ALP, he will obtain certificate and it is officially recognized equivalent to formal education completion.

Hassnain dreams to be happier with his family and be a person to contribute to his society. ALP supports him to make his dream come true by providing flexible learning opportunities.

title: 【Water×IoT】Innovation for Rural Water Supply in Africa【DMS + SUNDA】
text:
【Water×IoT】Innovation for Rural Water Supply in Africa【DMS + SUNDA】
Uganda's rural communities have been suffering from frequent breakdown of boreholes, due to lack of budget and capacity for proper operation and maintenance (O & M).

To solve these challenges, new innovative approaches are developed; "DMS" and "SUNDA".

"DMS" (Direct Management System) is a system in which an independent expertized organization provides timely and professional O & M of hand pump facilities in rural areas. 

"SUNDA" is an IoT "pay-as-you-fetch" prepaid system for hand pumps, which physically and psychologically enables fair contribution collection.

Result of the pilot project by Ministry of Water and Environment, Uganda and JICA collaboration with SUNDA Technology Global, 
 the amount of contribution collected DOUBLED
 caretakers free from heavy duties of money collection 
 users enjoy fairness, transparency and accountability of collected money

By covering 300 boreholes, DMS+SUNDA becomes financially self-sustaining. DMS+SUNDA can breakthrough structural challenges of rural water supply in developing countries.

JICA Development Studies Program (JICA-DSP) invites future leaders from partner countries to Japan and offers them the opportunity to learn about Japan’s modernization and development experience which differs from those of Europe and the U.S., and its wisdom as a country that provided cooperation toward the progress of developing countries after World War II. JICA-DSP is co-organized by various universities in Japan and JICA. Through those program, JICA hope that participants will gain a deep understanding of Japan, so that they may use this knowledge to contribute to the development of home countries. （Produced in March 2022）

title: Seminar "World Development Report 2022: Finance for an Equitable Recovery"
text:
Seminar "World Development Report 2022: Finance for an Equitable Recovery"
World Bank Group and JICA Ogata Research Institute hosted a seminar "World Development Report 2022: Finance for an Equitable Recovery" on May 11, 2022. 

At this seminar, Leora Klapper, WDR 2022 Director, Mahesh Uttamchandani, the Practice Manager for Financial Inclusion & Infrastructure in the Finance, Competitiveness, and Innovation Global Practice at the World Bank Group, and Beniamino Savonitto, an Economist in the Sector Economics and Development Impact department of the International Finance Corporation explained the main findings of the report. Yoshino Naoyuki, Professor Emeritus, Keio University, and Harada Tetsuya, Senior Executive Research Fellow, JICA Ogata Research Institute shared comments.

title: 【JICA with Bangladesh: Reaching 50th Year and Way Forward】Panel Discussion
text:
【JICA with Bangladesh: Reaching 50th Year and Way Forward】Panel Discussion
Soon after the independence of Bangladesh in 1971, Japan was one of the first countries to establish diplomatic relations on 10 February 1972. To commemorate the 50th Anniversary of that occasion, grand celebrations were held both in Dhaka and Tokyo. The collaborative relationship between Bangladesh and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) began in 1973 with the dispatching of Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers. In the context of this milestone year, the Embassy of Bangladesh in Japan, in collaboration with JICA, is holding the seminar to look back on the cooperation with JICA so far and to explore ways to further strengthen the partnership in the future. The seminar held on Friday, 10 June 2022.
This is Panel Discussion by Mr. Syed Nasir ERSHAD, Economic Minister, Bangladesh Embassy of Tokyo.

title: Knowledge forum: International student mobility and higher education during COVID-19
text:
Knowledge forum: International student mobility and higher education during COVID-19
The coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) has left no corner of our lives untouched, with higher education as no exception. As of April 2020, approximately 220 million tertiary students worldwide faced disruption to their education as universities temporarily closed due to the pandemic. Since then, as an emergency measure, classes have been widely held online in Japan and globally. Moreover, restrictions on international travel have greatly impacted students with plans to study abroad, forcing them to postpone or cancel their plans or change thei r study locations.

JICA Ogata Research Institute Knowledge Forum “International Student Mobility and Higher Education in the age of COVID-19: Reflections from Oxford University and the University of Tokyo” was held on January 18, 2022. Professor Kariya Takehiko of Oxford University and Professor Takahara Akio of the University of Tokyo discussed the current situation and challenges facing education at th ese two universities in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. They shared their visions for study abroad programs and university education both during the pandemic and in the post-COVID world.

title: Knowledge Forum: Diffusion of the Japanese Rice Farming Technologies to Asia a nd further to Africa
text:
Knowledge Forum: Diffusion of the Japanese Rice Farming Technologies to Asia a nd further to Africa
At this Knowledge Forum which was held March 22, 2022, Kobe University Professor Otsuka Keijiro, who has spent many years conducting research on development issues, focusing on agriculture in Asia and Africa, gave a lecture on the history of the transfer of rice farming technologies from Japan to Asia, and the possibility of the rice Green Revolution in Africa. We had an in-depth discussion with Otsuka regarding the major questions of what is important for bringing about the rice Green Revolution in Africa, and how JICA should support that. Note that Otsuka gave a lecture with the same title as this forum at the Imperial New Year's Lectures in January, 2022.

title: AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 1)
text:
AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 1)
JICA Ogata Research Institute and Africa Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD) Policy Bridge Tank jointly organized two book launch webinars on the theme of industrial development.

Session 1 of the webinar series shared the research findings from the book “Policy Learning for Industrial Development and the Role of Development Cooperation.” This volume contemplates Japanese development experiences that developi ng country’s policy makers can refer to when forming and implementing industr ial policies. The book also introduces development policy support, a type of J apanese intellectual cooperation aimed at providing hands-on policy advice and  promoting the learning process of partner countries through joint work. In th is webinar, authors of the book chapters presented their work and exchanged th oughts with AUDA-NEPAD discussants.

title: AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 2)
text:
AUDA-NEPAD and JICA Ogata Research Institute Joint Book Launch Webinar (Session 2)
JICA Ogata Research Institute and Africa Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD)  Policy Bridge Tank jointly organized two book launch webinars on the theme of  industrial development.

Session 2 of the webinar series shared the research findings from the book “Promoting Quality and Productivity Improvement/ Kaizen in Africa.” JICA began implementing various Kaizen projects in Africa since 2006. It has recently sta rted promoting the Africa Kaizen Initiative (AKI) in collaboration with the Af rican Union Development Agency - the New Partnership for Africa’s Development
 (AUDA-NEPAD) and the Pan-Africa Productivity Association (PAPA). This volume addresses how development cooperation to promote Kaizen can effectively suppor t the process of “translative adaptation” by partner countries. In this webinar, authors of the book chapters presented their work and exchanged thoughts with African discussants.

Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion (SHEP) Approach have developed in Kenya through technical cooperation project by JICA which started from 2006 and succeeded in increasing farmers' income.  It aims to improve farmers' income by changing their mindset from "grow and sell" to "grow to sell" and improving their farming and cultivation skills.
This video is an interview with farmers who participated in the Market Survey, Stakeholder forum, Family budgeting, and Demand-driven technical training, which are part of the SHEP approach training.

text:
Voix d'agriculteurs - Interviews d'agriculteurs ayant participé à la formation SHEP (JICA SENEGAL)
L'approche SHEP (Smallholder Horticulture Empowerment & Promotion) s'est développée au Kenya en 2006 grâce à un projet de coopération technique de la JICA et a permis d'augmenter les revenus des agriculteurs.  L’approche SHEP vise à améliorer les revenus des agriculteurs en changeant leur mentalité de "produire et vendre" à "produire pour vendre" et en améliorant leurs compétences agricoles et culturales.
Cette vidéo est une interview d'agriculteurs ayant participé à l'étude de marché, au forum de rencontre, à la caisse familiale et à la formation technique axée sur la demande, qui font partie de la formation de l'approche SHEP.

title: JICA Chair Special Lecture ‘Japan after World War II and Japan-China Relations in the Modern Era’
text:
JICA Chair Special Lecture ‘Japan after World War II and Japan-China Relations in the Modern Era’
In order to expand the opportunities of Japanese studies in developing countries, JICA launched the “JICA Chair (JICA Program for Japanese studies)” in collaboration with leading universities in partner countries. On March 22, 2022, the opening ceremony for JICA Chair program was held at the University of Belgrade, Serbia. More than 100 participants, mainly the students of the Faculty of Philology at the University, attended. After the ceremony, Prof. Akio Takahara, the executive director of JICA Ogata Research Institute, delivered a special lecture on how Japan's foreign policy and Japan-China relations have changed since the end of World War II and the Cold War.

text:

Within the framework of the project "School for All: Project for Improvement in Basic Education Quality and Girl-Boy Parity through School-Community Collaboration", JICA has produced 3 documentary films whose main actors are: the members of the SMC, the teacher and the pupil at the basic education level, and each in the regions of Zinder, Maradi and Tahoua with the title "The Challenges that create the future".

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - MRT "Restoring Hope for the Cities"
text:
Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - MRT "Restoring Hope for the Cities"
MRT Jakarta Phase 1's project, from Lebak Bulus to Bundaran HI stretches for 15.7 km, was built with funding from Japan through ODA loan program, with the assistance of JICA. MRT Jakarta is the first underground train In Indonesia, which its operation started in March 2019. Constructed in the heart and capital of Indonesia, Jakarta, this project was initiated to solve the problem of traffic congestion, and also expected to improve the people's quality of life, able to move the wheels of the economy, and restore dreams for the residents of this city.

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Patimban Port "Connecting Economical Veins"
text:
Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Patimban Port "Connecting Economical Veins"
Patimban Port is a collaboration project between the Government of Japan and Indonesia through JICA. Build on a land of 654 acres in Subang, West Java, Patimban Port is currently one of the largest port in Indonesia. This port, connected to the toll road and several priority industrial areas, such as Bekasi, Karawang, and Purwakarta is expected to become one of the veins in world trading, and to be the key link between industry, as well as supporting acceleration of export-import sector.

title: Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Transportation Sector "Building the Future"
text:
Indonesia-Japan Collabonations - Transportation Sector "Building the Future"
The collaboration between JICA and Indonesia has been going for more than 60 years, with supports on Indonesia's development in various fields, including the transportation and logistic sector. JICA takes part in accelerating various mega tranportation and logistic projects in Indonesia, including the construction of MRT Jakarta, Patimban Port, the development of several international airports such as Ngurah Rai Airport in Bali and Juanda Airport in Surabaya, and also the construction and expansion of Merak-Bakaheuni Ferry Terminal.

title: 【JICA DX】Concept Movie
text:
【JICA DX】Concept Movie
This is a movie on JICA’s partnership approach on digital development. It shows the case of Melody International Ltd., a Japanese health-tech start-up company working on maternal and child health. The product "Melody i" is a cloud-type mobile fetal monitor and perinatal e-Health platform that allows doctors to view data and communicate their diagnosis with pregnant women from distance.
In JICA’s global agenda for Digital for Development, we are seeking innovative solutions and technologies to add values that can be combined with our tested conventional methods.  We welcome collaboration with other partners to achieve our goal, "digital transformation to improve well-being for all."

title: 【JICA DX】Partner Interview (Melody International Ltd.)
text:
【JICA DX】Partner Interview (Melody International Ltd.)
To contribute to digital development in JICA's partner countries, it is essential to collaborate with partner organizations/companies with advanced technologies and innovative ideas. This video introduces an example of JICA's approach for digital for development along with an interview story of Melody International Ltd, an Japanese start-up that works on maternal and child health issues in Thailand and Bhutan. JICA works for digital development by co-creation with various partners.

title: 【JICA-PRESSMN】La mise en œuvre des soins de maternité et de néonatal respectueux
text:
【JICA-PRESSMN】La mise en œuvre des soins de maternité et de néonatal respectueux
C’est le résumé d’un film documentaire à travers des témoignages d'acteurs de santé sénégalais, l’historique et les expériences de la coopération entre le Japon et le Sénégal en mise en pratique des soins respectueux dans le cadre du PRESSMN (Projet de Renforcement des Soins de Santé Maternelle et Néonatale). 

Le Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action Sociale, en partenariat avec la JICA, a créé le PRESSMN en 2009. Depuis, le PRESSMN poursuit ses efforts pour améliorer la qualité des soins et la disponibilité des services de santé maternelle et néonatale afin de contribuer à la réduction du taux de mortalité maternelle et néonatale au Sénégal. 

La version complète est aussi disponible sur cette chaine.

title: A story of Friendship and Assistance
text:
A story of Friendship and Assistance
A Story of Friendship and Assitance

This short animated film is the story of a girl named Areeba Saleha, born to a family hailing from Abbottabad, Pakistan. Her lifelong friendship with JICA started with her birth at the Children's Hospital in Islamabad. Areeba's parents raised her through thick and thin, but JICA's assistance in health, disaster management, education, and water and sanitation, at every step of the way, did befriend her. Today, Areeba has set up her own fashion apparel brand and is a role model for many children like her who deserve a good life. Her story embodies JICA's vision and mission of decades of partnership with the people of Pakistan.

title: COVID-19 Webinar Series #10 “Building Health Systems toward Resilient UHC with/after the Pandemic”
text:
COVID-19 Webinar Series #10 “Building Health Systems toward Resilient UHC with/after the Pandemic”
In order to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic and sustain other health services, countries have been required to rapidly increase and reorganize health service delivery capacity, such as availability of hospital beds, allocation of health human resource and so on. Some countries may have had a legal framework or policy tool to enable such rapid increase, and others may have taken other approaches to deliver the services efficiently and equitably under the resource limited situation, such as remote services. However, it has not been sufficiently clear how countries took actions.

In the 10th JICA COVID-19 Webinar, we listened to different countries’ experience and lessons of preparedness and adaption of health service delivery to cope with COVID-19 and other health needs, and discussed what implications this experience has for the efforts to achieve resilient UHC with and after the Pandemic.

title: Theory of Change - A Roadmap for Development Goals
text:

The video takes the ToC approach with an example of the Angolan Maternal and Child Health Handbook Project in which JICA has assisted, and unfolds how the Project has changed the behaviors of pregnant women and mothers, ultimately contributing to the SDG3: Good Health and Well-being. The video aims to visualize the pathways of development effects through ToC.

Como se crearon los materiales educativos ESMATE, quienes participan y como funcionaron durante la pandemia de COVID-19.

title: Proyecto ESMATE y la pandemia de COVID-19 (VIDEO 4 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
text:
Proyecto ESMATE y la pandemia de COVID-19 (VIDEO 4 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
En 2020, a pesar que “Proyecto ESMATE” había terminado en junio de 2019, el Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador continuó actualizando, imprimiendo y distribuyendo los materiales educativos de ESMATE, lo que permitió facilitar el proceso de transición de clases presenciales a clases virtuales asegurando la continuidad de la enseñanza de los niños y niñas salvadoreños. En este video, que la cuarta y última parte de los videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE, te presentamos los usos y ventajas que tuvieron los materiales ESMATE durante la pandemia de COVID-19 gracias al liderazgo y visión del Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador.

title: Proyecto ESMATE, más que solo materiales educativos (VIDEO 3 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
text:
Proyecto ESMATE, más que solo materiales educativos (VIDEO 3 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
La elaboración y actualización de los materiales educativos producidos por el “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media - ESMATE” han implicado desde el inicio en 2015, todo un proceso de seguimiento y evaluación en el cual participan docentes, directores, técnicos entre otros. En esta tercera entrega de cuatro videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE, te presentamos el proceso técnico detrás del uso de los materiales educativos de ESMATE.

title: Proyecto ESMATE y sus materiales educativos (VIDEO 2 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
text:
Proyecto ESMATE y sus materiales educativos (VIDEO 2 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
El “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media”, mejor conocido como “Proyecto ESMATE”, entre 2015 y 2019, elaboró 3 materiales educativos principales: Libros de texto, cuadernos de ejercicios y guías metodológica de primer grado a bachillerato. Para conocer más, sobre el proceso de elaboración y el uso de cada material educativo, te presentamos el segundo video de cuadro especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE y su continuidad a la fecha. Continua pendiente de nuestras siguientes publicaciones para seguir viendo más.

title: Proyecto ESMATE, un esfuerzo que inició en 2015 (VIDEO 1 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
text:
Proyecto ESMATE, un esfuerzo que inició en 2015 (VIDEO 1 / JICA EL SALVADOR)
En 2015, junto con el Ministerio de Educación de El Salvador, iniciamos la ejecución del “Proyecto de Mejoramiento de los Aprendizajes de Matemática en Educación Básica y Educación Media”, mejor conocido como “Proyecto ESMATE”. Aunque el proyecto finalizó en junio de 2019, sus resultados siguen trascendiendo en la educación de los niños y niñas salvadoreños. Este día, la oficina de JICA lanza la presentación de 1 de 4 videos especialmente elaborados para darte a conocer más sobre ESMATE y su continuidad a la fecha.

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #2 "Japan’s Public Health Approach for COVID-19 - past, present, and future-"
text:
JICA COVID-19 Webinar #2 "Japan’s Public Health Approach for COVID-19 - past, present, and future-"
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series brings together leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. This is the 2nd webinar and we will invite Prof. Hitoshi Oshitani as a speaker. Prof. Hitoshi Oshitani; MD, MPH, PhD, is a Professor at Department of Virology, Tohoku University Graduate School of Medicine, Japan; a member of the Subcommittee on Novel Coronavirus Disease Control under the Japanese government Advisory Council. Between 1999 and 2005 Prof. Oshitani was an Infectious Diseases Control Advisor at the WHO’s Regional Office for the Western Pacific, the Philippines, during which he coordinated the response to SARS. 

Webinar Structure
 - introduction (5min)
 - Presentation by Prof.Oshitani (40 min)
 - Q&A, discussion (40 min)
 - Closing (5 min)

title: [KCCP] Non-Revenue Water Management (Leakage Control)
text:
[KCCP] Non-Revenue Water Management (Leakage Control)
The water leakage rates in distribution networks are considerably high in developing countries. It can be the potential cause of water contamination, low water pressure and intermittent water supply. The aim of this program is to obtain and upgrade knowledge and technical skills on non-revenue water management. On 4th February, 12 participants joined the field work session, held in Training and Technical Development Center, Bureau of Waterworks, Tokyo Metropolitan Government. The participants first studied the Leakage Prevention and Waterworks Mapping System in Tokyo. Afterwards, they experienced the practical field work based on the lecture content. 
　　　　　　　　　　　 　　
Place: Training and Technical Development Center, Bureau of Waterworks, Tokyo Metropolitan Government

Le projet SHEP au Kenya a promu des activités «Do-nou». Les agriculteurs peuvent réparer eux-mêmes leur route en utilisant Do-nou. Avant d'utiliser Do-nou, Quand il pleut, la route devient une grande flaque. Cependant, Do-nou aide à garder la route en bon état pendant une longue période, il est également facile de réparer par eux-mêmes. Lorsque le fermier vend ses produits ou les acheteurs, visitez les lieux des agriculteurs pour acheter les produits, la bonne route aide toujours. However, Do-nou helps to keep the road in a good condition for a long time, also it is easy to fix by themselves. When the farmer sell their products or buyers visit the farmers' places to buy the products, the good road always helps. http://coreroad.org/Community Road Empowerment

title: A video message from Dr. Kitaoka, president of JICA to celebrate the initiation of "JICA Chair"
text:
A video message from Dr. Kitaoka, president of JICA to celebrate the initiation of "JICA Chair"
JICA launched the "JICA Development Studies Program" in 2018 to provide future leaders of developing countries with opportunities to not only receive education and pursue research in Japan, but also to learn about Japan's modernization experience. As one part of this programme, JICA started "JICA Chair" to share our country's experience and knowledge with JICA partners especially targeting the top universities in developing countries. 

This video message is released by Shinichi Kitaoka, the president of JICA, for celebrating the initiation and the holding of innovative JICA Chair Program in the Latin America and the Caribbean region.

JICA's vision is "Leading the World with Trust." We believe forging trust between countries is more critical now than ever before. With trust at the core of our cooperation, JICA implements its programs with partner countries on the basis of mutual understanding and respect - not from an unequal footing characterized by “aid” or “assistance.”

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #6 "Response to COVID-19 by Public Health Centers in Japan"
text:
JICA COVID-19 Webinar #6 "Response to COVID-19 by Public Health Centers in Japan"
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series starting January 2021 brings together various leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. The webinar is intended primarily for health professionals in low- and middle-income countries. In this 6th webinar, we will invite two directors of Public Health Centers (“hokenjo” in Japanese) as guest speakers. Dr YOMO, Akihiro, Director, Fukui Prefectural Public health Center, will give an overview of public health system in Japan and the role of public health centers, as well as the COVID-19 response during pandemic In Japan. Dr TSURUGI, Yoko, Director, Kikuchi Prefectural Public Health Center, Kumamoto Prefecture, will present various cases of specific COVID-19 measures at public health centers. [Program] Opening Remarks & Introduction of Speakers MAKIMOTO, Saeda, JICA Ogata Research Institute for Peace and Development Presentation by Dr YOMO, Akihiro “Japanese local health system and roles of public health centers” Presentation by Dr TSURUGI, Yoko “PHC and specific cases of Covid-19 in Japan” Q&A

title: Webinar on Changing Landscape of Development Cooperation in Southeast Asia
text:
Webinar on Changing Landscape of Development Cooperation in Southeast Asia
In this webinar, we would shed light on the realities of development cooperation in Southeast Asian region with an emphasis on the analysis of South-South Cooperation (SSC) by the “emerging donors” in the region. Specifically, Thailand’s endeavor to be a more active regional provider of development cooperation, Indonesia’s recent move to establish its streamlined aid agency (Indonesian AID), and Vietnam’s emergence as a provider of SSC to neighboring states, are discussed.

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar #5 "How Ag-RDTs will change the course of COVID-19 pandemic"
text:
JICA COVID-19 Webinar #5 "How Ag-RDTs will change the course of COVID-19 pandemic"
In the 5th JICA COVID-19 Webinar, we focused on the role and effective use of antigen-detecting rapid diagnostic tests (Ag-RDTs) for COVID-19. We invited Prof. YANAGIHARA Katsunori, MD.,Ph.D, Nagasaki University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences in Japan, as a keynote speaker to present experience in the use of Ag-RDTs in Japan. Afterward, as an introduction to the Ag-RDTs approved in Japan, Mr. Oi of FUJIFILM Corporation introduced an antigen test kit that uses silver amplification technology. Program: -Housekeeping & Opening Remarks (10min) -“The role and effective use of Ag-RDTs for COVID-19 and experience in the use of Ag-RDTs in Japan” (20min) Presentation by Prof. YANAGIHARA Katsunori -“Japanese technology and approved Ag-RDTs FUJIFILM COVID-19 Ag Test” (10min) Presentation by OI Koji -“Collaborative Effort of JICA and LMICs on COVID-19 testing” (5min) Presentation by Dr. ISONO Mitsuo -Q&A Session (30min)

title: Knowledge Forum 'Tackling Extreme Climate Events Around the World'
text:
Knowledge Forum 'Tackling Extreme Climate Events Around the World'
Efforts to address climate change continue to accelerate regardless of the COVID-19 pandemic. During the plenary meetings of the UN General Assembly in September 2020, many states made announcements on their roadmaps to reduce carbon dioxide emission and to achieve carbon neutrality. Moreover, extreme climate events such as torrential rain, floods and heatwaves are frequently occurring around the world, and it has been reported that global warming is one major cause of these. Under such circumstances, measures for climate change adaptation are increasingly seen to be important, along with those for climate change mitigation that aim to reduce carbon dioxide emission. Meanwhile, many challenges remain in identifying what programs could lead to adaptation. Currently, efforts are moving forward by further developing existing programs. In this forum, Mimura Nobuo, distinguished fellow at the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development (JICA Ogata Research Institute) and specially appointed professor at the Global and Local Environment Co-creation Institute of Ibaraki University, gave a keynote speech about domestic and international trends in current efforts for climate change adaptation. The content of the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6 by the IPCC Working Group II), which is to be published in 2022, and discussions that took place in COP26 will be covered as well. Mimura also made recommendations for Japan’s roles in global collaboration. Furthermore, based on

title: JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series #7 "To Realize Unknowns About COVID-19 Vaccines"
text:
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series #7 "To Realize Unknowns About COVID-19 Vaccines"
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series starting January 2021 brings together various leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. The webinar is intended primarily for health professionals in low- and middle-income countries. The 7th Webinar focuses on COVID-19 Vaccines. We receive various information on vaccines but do we understand them correctly? The guest speaker, Dr Nakayama will provide lecture on the essential and latest knowledge on COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Webinar #8 How Can We Rapidly and Efficiently Optimize the Best Therapeutic Management for COVID-19?
text:
Webinar #8 How Can We Rapidly and Efficiently Optimize the Best Therapeutic Management for COVID-19?
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series starting January 2021 brings together various leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. The webinar is intended primarily for health professionals in low- and middle-income countries. In this 8th webinar, we focused on the innovative trial design to rapidly and efficiently evaluate multiple interventions to optimize the best therapeutics for COVID-19: REMAP-CAP (Randomized, Embedded, Multifactorial, Adaptive Platform trial for Community-Acquired Pneumonia). We invited three guest speakers from Japan, Nepal and Pakistan, who are involved in REMAP-CAP trial in their country, to discuss common features of APTs (Adaptive Platform Trials) and share the experience of REMAP-CAP launching and expanding in the country.

title: Seminar "World Development Report 2021: Data for Better Lives"
text:
Seminar "World Development Report 2021: Data for Better Lives"
The World Bank Group has published its World Development Report (WDR) annually since 1978. Each release addresses timely topics in the areas of economy, society, and the environment and puts forward policy recommendations. On March 24, 2021, the World Bank Group published the "World Development Report 2021: Data for Better Lives." At a webinar held in July 27, 2021, Vivien Foster, a co-director of the WDR and chief economist for the Infrastructure Vice-Presidency of the World Bank; Dean Jolliffe, a co-director of the WDR and lead economist of the Development Data Group at the World Bank; and Malarvizhi Veerappan, WDR2021 manager and senior data scientist of the Development Data Group at the World Bank; will provide an overview of the report. Makino Koji, Deputy Director of JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development and Ito Seiro, Director, Microeconomic Analysis Studies Group, Development Studies Center, JETRO-Institute of Developing Economies will give comments on the report.

title: Spillover Effects on Urban Transformation
text:
Spillover Effects on Urban Transformation
JICA Ogata Research Institute is working together with the Infrastructure Management Department of JICA, to leverage spillover effects of urban transportation infrastructure development. The objectives of this explanatory video are to promote the idea of the spillover effect of infrastructure development and its potential use in infrastructure finance, and to help promote dialogue and concrete collaborations among practitioners in Japan and developing countries. Suzuki Tomoyoshi, a research fellow at JICA Ogata Research Institute, and Kawahashi Takehiro, a member of the Infrastructure Management Department of JICA, provide an explanation of spillover effects. In addition, Yoshino Naoyuki, director of the Financial Research Center of the Financial Services Agency of Japan, explains their importance. JICA緒方貞子平和開発研究所（JICA緒方研究所）は、JICA社会基盤部と共同で、都市交通インフラの整備によって生じるスピルオーバー効果の活用に向けて取り組みを進めています。 このたび、こうしたインフラ開発のスピルオーバー効果とそのインフラファイナンスへの活用の可能性について、考え方の普及を進め、日本国内および開発途上国の実務者との対話や具体的な連携促進に役立つように解説動画を制作しました。 JICA緒方研究所の鈴木智良研究員とJICA社会基盤部の川端剛弘職員がスピルオーバー効果を分かりやすく説明するほか、吉野直行金融庁金融研究センター長がその重要性についても解説します。

title: [Knowledge Forum] Reforming the International System to Make the COVID-19 the Last Pandemic
text:
[Knowledge Forum] Reforming the International System to Make the COVID-19 the Last Pandemic
In this Knowledge Forum, Dr. MABUCHI Shunsuke, who was the only Asian participant in the work of the Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response (IPPPR) as a member of the secretariat, introduced the contents and process of the IPPPR's report, the discussions within the IPPPR and with the stakeholders on the report and its recommendations. The aim of this forum was to provide opportunities to discuss the reform of the international system and the future of Japan's international cooperation policies and the development programs with all participants. *The speeches were translated from Japanese into English by simultaneous interpreters.

title: Human Security in Mindanao, the Philippines, Advocated by Former JICA President Ogata Sadako
text:
Human Security in Mindanao, the Philippines, Advocated by Former JICA President Ogata Sadako
Ogata Sadako, who served as the president of JICA for approximately ten years, promoted “human security,” the idea of creating a world where all people can live in dignity, free from fear and want. This video explains the meaning of human security, which Ogata had espoused, as well as the sorts of cooperative efforts JICA has engaged in to make human security a reality, while introducing a case of Mindanao, the Philippines.

title: #4 "Detecting Predictive Biomarkers for Severe COVID-19 – the Latest Research Findings from Japan"
text:
#4 "Detecting Predictive Biomarkers for Severe COVID-19 – the Latest Research Findings from Japan"
In this 4th JICA COVID-19 Webinar, we focus on the latest developments of research on biomarkers that predict if COVID-19 patients get severe symptoms. We will invite Dr. SUGIYAMA Masaya and Dr. NOIRI Eisei, senior scientists at NCGM (National Center for Global Health and Medicine) in Japan, to present their research work on predictive biomarkers identified from blood and urine samples, respectively. The movie is in French, with no subtitles. To view in English, please use YouTube’s automatic subtitles feature (Click the subtitles button and then click the Settings button to select English).

title: Memorial Symposium for the Late Ogata Sadako (Condensed Version) (November 2020)
text:
Memorial Symposium for the Late Ogata Sadako (Condensed Version) (November 2020)
On Nov. 2, 2020, the JICA Ogata Sadako Research Institute for Peace and Development hosted an online symposium entitled “Embracing Human Security in Meeting Global Challenges in the COVID-19/Post-COVID-19 Era” in commemoration of the first-year anniversary of the passing of Ogata Sadako, former United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and former JICA President. International dignitaries, including António Guterres, secretary-general of the United Nations, Filippo Grandi, the United Nations high commissioner for Refugees, and Ashraf Ghani, the president of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan, sent video messages to commemorate the achievements and relive the legacy of Ogata. Moreover, a distinguished panel of scholars and experts discussed how human security, a concept that Ogata passionately advocated, can be applied to the battle against the COVID-19 pandemic. The video is a condensed and edited version of the symposium.

title: Interview  “Adaptive peacebuilding” with Cedric de Coning, NUPI
text:
Interview  “Adaptive peacebuilding” with Cedric de Coning, NUPI
While conducting peacebuilding activities, we try a range of different options to learn from the process and accordingly adapt, because we don’t know beforehand what will work and what will not, says Cedric de Coning, a senior research fellow of the Research Group on Peace, Conflict, and Development at the Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (NUPI). Cedric de Coning has named this approach “adaptive peacebuilding,” and he posits it as a potentially effective alternative to the conventional blueprint or top-down practice that has failed over decades of efforts to build peace in conflict stricken communities. When he visited JICA Research Institute in September 2019, we also sought de Coning’s opinions on the contributions of rising peacebuilding actors and on the role of development agencies toward the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Interview: “Challenges Faced While Helping Male Victims of Sexual Violence” with Chris Dolan, RLP
text:
Interview: “Challenges Faced While Helping Male Victims of Sexual Violence” with Chris Dolan, RLP
The difficulties in helping male victims of gender-based violence (GBV) in conflict situations arise from the traditional norms of masculinity and femininity and from the assumption that if a man is a victim of sexual violence, his masculinity is questionable, says Chris Dolan, director of the Refugee Law Project (RLP) . These assumptions, he asserts, are true both for survivors themselves as well as for the organizations that should be supporting them. This thought holds the victims back from talking about what happened. We got a chance to interview him when he visited the JICA Research Institute for the seminar “Gender-Based Violence (GBV) in the Conflict-affected Areas: Lessons from the Case of Refugee Settlement in Uganda and Japan” in August 2019.

title: "Human Security and Cross-Border Cooperation in East Asia" by Yoichi Mine (September 28, 2018)
text:
"Human Security and Cross-Border Cooperation in East Asia" by Yoichi Mine (September 28, 2018)
How is the concept of human security perceived in East Asia and how can human security in practice be realized in that region? Yoichi Mine, visiting fellow at JICA Research Institute, presented at an open symposium the findings of a research conducted by the JICA Research Institute, which has published a book titled “Human Security and Cross-Border Cooperation in East Asia” as the outcome of the research. The symposium “The Practices of Human Security in the ASEAN+3: Recommendations from Academics and Practitioners” was held in Tokyo on September 28, 2018.

title: Presentation 'Economic and Social Development of Bangladesh' by Yasuyuki Sawada (August 27, 2018)
text:
Presentation 'Economic and Social Development of Bangladesh' by Yasuyuki Sawada (August 27, 2018)
At a launch event for the book “Economic and Social Development of Bangladesh: Miracle and Challenges,” Yasuyuki Sawada, chief economist at the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and former JICA-RI visiting fellow, gave an overview of the book. Sawada discussed factors affecting the development of Bangladesh based on empirical analysis. The book is the product of a three-year research project entitled “Empirical Study on Risk and Poverty in Bangladesh,” conducted by the JICA Research Institute (JICA-RI).

title: ‘Transforming our world' — Part II   Discussion with Jeffrey Sachs November 29, 2017
text:
‘Transforming our world' — Part II   Discussion with Jeffrey Sachs November 29, 2017
*Audio contains English and Japanese speakers. A world in which each country thinks that cooperation is not possible and chooses to look at itself in isolation will be a very dangerous world, says Jeffrey Sachs, professor at Columbia University, in light of the rising nationalism around the world. Everybody talks to each other even if they do not like each other at all, that is the art of diplomacy and is of extraordinary importance because it is the only way to keep peace, he emphasized. During a lecture delivered by Sachs at a seminar hosted by Sophia University and JICA-RI, he discussed global issues and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with the audience.

title: Presentation 'JICA's activities in Bangladesh' by Shohei Hara (August 27, 2018)
text:
Presentation 'JICA's activities in Bangladesh' by Shohei Hara (August 27, 2018)
At a launch event for the book “Economic and Social Development of Bangladesh: Miracle and Challenges,” Shohei Hara, director general, South Asia Department, Japan International Cooperation Agency, gave a presentation on JICA’s activities in Bangladesh. The book is the product of a three-year research project entitled “Empirical Study on Risk and Poverty in Bangladesh,” conducted by the JICA Research Institute (JICA-RI).

title: Presentation 'ADB's strategy for operation in Bangladesh' by Manmohan Parkash (August 27, 2018)
text:
Presentation 'ADB's strategy for operation in Bangladesh' by Manmohan Parkash (August 27, 2018)
At a launch event for the book “Economic and Social Development of Bangladesh: Miracle and Challenges,” Manmohan Parkash, country director, Bangladesh Resident Mission, Asia Development Bank, gave a presentation on ADB’s strategy for operations in Bangladesh. The book is the product of a three-year research project entitled “Empirical Study on Risk and Poverty in Bangladesh,” conducted by the JICA Research Institute (JICA-RI).

title: Interview  'Statistical Capacity for Monitoring SDGs,' with Ryuichi Tomizawa, JICA
text:
Interview  'Statistical Capacity for Monitoring SDGs,' with Ryuichi Tomizawa, JICA
Ryuichi Tomizawa, deputy director general, Procurement Department, the Japan International Cooperation Agency, contributed a chapter to the book From Summits to Solutions: Innovations in Implementing the Sustainable Development Goals, which is the product of joint research undertaken by the Brookings Institution and the JICA Research Institute. Tomizawa co-authored Chapter 9, “Enhancing Statistical Capacity for Development,” with Noriharu Masugi, who is also a staff member of JICA. While summarizing the chapter, Tomizawa emphasized the need for each country to improve its capacity of producing and disseminating statistical data to monitor the progress of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Interview with David Malone, director of the United Nations University
text:
Interview with David Malone, director of the United Nations University
Interview with David Malone, director of the United Nations University. As an editor, he introduced the book "International Development: Ideas, Experience, and Prospects" published in February 2014. Reviewing theories and methodologies in development, he outlined the future prospects on development based on his own experience.

title: Interview  ' Partnerships for Global Health Governance,' with Ikuo Takizawa, JICA
text:
Interview  ' Partnerships for Global Health Governance,' with Ikuo Takizawa, JICA
Ikuo Takizawa, deputy director general, Human Development Department, the Japan International Cooperation Agency, contributed a chapter to the book, “From Summits to Solutions: Innovations in Implementing the Sustainable Development Goals,” which is the product of joint research undertaken by the Brookings Institution and the JICA Research Institute. Takizawa wrote Chapter 15 entitled, “Unity in Diversity: Reshaping the Global Health Architecture.” In summarizing the chapter, Takizawa discussed partnerships for global health governance under the Sustainable Development Goals Framework.

title: 'Managing Global Governance'—A presentation by Li Xiaoyun October 3, 2017
text:
'Managing Global Governance'—A presentation by Li Xiaoyun October 3, 2017
In contrast with country development that entails the concept of a nation state or a legitimate form of sovereignty, global development requires trans-boundary cooperation. Li Xiaoyun, Professor at China Agricultural University’s College of Humanities and Development, emphasizes the need to develop joint capacity in order to achieve global development and tackle common challenges. Li provided his views on managing global governance at a seminar entitled, "German Strategic Engagement for Creating Network with Emerging Countries: Learning from Experiences of Managing Global Governance (MGG) " held at JICA-RI on October 3, 2017.

title: Interview with Surin Pitsuwan, Distinguished Fellow, JICA Research Institute
text:
Interview with Surin Pitsuwan, Distinguished Fellow, JICA Research Institute
Interview with Former ASEAN Secretary-General Surin Pitsuwan Surin Pitsuwan, now Distinguished Fellow of JICA Research Institute. He talks about ASEAN and Japan's contribution, importance of enphasizing human development and human security, and more,

title: Field Trip to South India Sheds Light on JICA's Achievements
text:
Field Trip to South India Sheds Light on JICA's Achievements
Field trip to South India for writing a Project History book on India's silk industry. The book is available in Japanese only. https://www.jica.go.jp/jica-ri/ja/publication/projecthistory/siruku_taikoku_indo_ni_keishosareta_nippon_no_yousan_no_waza.html

title: 'Transforming our world' — Part I  A presentation by Jeffrey Sachs November 29, 2017
text:
'Transforming our world' — Part I  A presentation by Jeffrey Sachs November 29, 2017
In the face of an array of mounting global problems—from climate change induced disasters to poverty and education—how can the world deal with such issues? Jeffrey Sachs, professor at Columbia University, says that learning and cooperating with others is essential and that we together need to ensure sustainable development on priority. Sachs delivered a presentation at a seminar hosted by Sophia University and JICA-RI, during his visit to Japan in November, 2017.

title: Interview with Mari Katayanagi, Senior Research Fellow, JICA Research Institute
text:
Interview with Mari Katayanagi, Senior Research Fellow, JICA Research Institute
Interview with Mari Katayanagi, Senior Research Fellow, JICA Research Institute. She introduces the book "Preventing Violent Conflict in Africa: Inequalities, Perceptions and Institutions", which she contributed in its publication. https://www.jica.go.jp/jica-ri/publication/booksandreports/preventing_violent_conflict_in_africa_inequalities_perceptions_and_institutions.html

title: 'Creating Networks with Southern Powers'— Thomas Fues, DIE October 3, 2017
text:
'Creating Networks with Southern Powers'— Thomas Fues, DIE October 3, 2017
While the tide of development cooperation is shifting from aid provision to collaboration, what will be the next approach to make the collaboration successful? Thomas Fues, Head of the Training Department, German Development Institute (DIE), presents the challenges and the way forward for the collaboration by referring to the Managing Global Governance (MGG) programme, a German training scheme for young professionals from emerging countries. A movie about the MGG Program shown in his presentation can be viewed at the following location: www.youtube.com/embed/OZl154JWTDQ (9 mins). Fues visited JICA-RI for a seminar held on October 3, 2017.

title: Interview with John Humphrey, professor at the University of Sussex
text:
Interview with John Humphrey, professor at the University of Sussex
Interview with John Humphrey, professor at the University of Sussex. He talks about the role of China, value-chain approach, and more.

title: Interview  'Quality data for citizens,' with Wah Wah Maung, the Central Statistical Organization
text:
Interview  'Quality data for citizens,' with Wah Wah Maung, the Central Statistical Organization
In Myanmar, where seven out of ten people use smart phone, mobile phone, the way forward is to improve quality data, says Wah Wah Maung, Director General, the Central Statistical Organization, Ministry of Planning and Finance of Myanmar. She also talked about the use of data technologies for the achievement of SDGs. We interviewed her when she visited JICA-RI for the public seminar on the CSIS-JICA RI joint research project in September, 2017.

title: Seminar on the Normative Framework of Japan’s ODA by Sakiko Fukuda Parr
text:
Seminar on the Normative Framework of Japan’s ODA by Sakiko Fukuda Parr
Sakiko Fukuda-Parr, distinguished fellow at the JICA Research Institute and a professor at The New School, U.S., delivered a lecture "Normative Framework of Development Cooperation: Japanese aid between the DAC and Southern donors" at the JICA Ichigaya Building in Tokyo on January 17, 2017. Fukuda-Parr explained that the Japanese aid model emphasizes the mutual benefits and respect for sovereignty in donor–recipient relationships in contrast to the OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) donors' "aid as charity."

title: Interview  'Data technologies for supporting developing countries,' with Haishan Fu,  the World Bank
text:
Interview  'Data technologies for supporting developing countries,' with Haishan Fu,  the World Bank
“We already know that a lot of good data technologies exist, it’s just not evenly distributed across the world,” says Haishan Fu, the Director of the Development Data Group, World Bank. She spoke about how the World Bank has been working toward supporting low-income countries in leveraging data technologies. We interviewed her when she visited JICA-RI for the public seminar on the CSIS-JICA RI joint research project in September, 2017.

title: Interview: 'New aspect of Japanese aid strategies,' with David Arase, the Hopkins-Nanjing Center
text:
Interview: 'New aspect of Japanese aid strategies,' with David Arase, the Hopkins-Nanjing Center
Japanese aid strategies have traditionally been infrastructure-export oriented and focused on Asia, but this has changed with the establishment of the 2015 Development Cooperation Charter, says David Arase, professor of international politics at the Hopkins-Nanjing Center for Chinese and American Studies. He says that Japan's development cooperation will be more closely tied to the country’s interest and that this will contribute to not only global welfare but also wider issues of international stability and peace.

title: 'The data revolution for SDGs'—A presentation by Daniel F. Runde (September 19, 2017)
text:
'The data revolution for SDGs'—A presentation by Daniel F. Runde (September 19, 2017)
Daniel F. Runde, Director of the Project on Prosperity and Development, Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), says Japan has a critical role to play in achieving a data revolution for development. Runde delivered a presentation at the JICA Ichigaya Building, Tokyo, on September 19, 2017, on the occasion of the launch of the joint report of the CSIS and the JICA Research Institute. The report was entitled “Harnessing the Data Revolution to Achieve the Sustainable Development Goals: Enabling Frogs to Leap.”

title: "2016 Human Development Report - Human Development for Everyone" by Selim Jahan (May 18, 2017)
text:
"2016 Human Development Report - Human Development for Everyone" by Selim Jahan (May 18, 2017)
Selim Jahan, Director of Human Development Report Office, UNDP, delivered a keynote speech at JICA Research Institute to introduce the background and contents of the 2016 Human Development Report.

title: Interview  'Impact evaluations in modern development economics' with Yasuyuki Sawada
text:
Interview  'Impact evaluations in modern development economics' with Yasuyuki Sawada
Development Economics, a field once relegated to the brink of extinction, was substantially revived as a top field of economics because of its field experiment revolution, says Yasuyuki Sawada, the JICA Research Institute Visiting Fellow, who is also a professor at the University of Tokyo. Sawada added that the field experiment revolution has given rise to various techniques for the precise evaluation of causal impact of interventions, which used to be evaluated only softly due to lack of evidence. He has shared some of his findings on the impact of evaluation projects at JICA-RI. He has been appointed as the Chief Economist at the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and is expected to assume office in the spring of 2017.

title: Interview  “Inclusive education will improve the quality of education,” with Kazuo Kuroda, JICA RI
text:
Interview  “Inclusive education will improve the quality of education,” with Kazuo Kuroda, JICA RI
The number of “out of school children” in the world is estimated to be around 60 million. It is said that one-third of them are children with disabilities at the primary school level and only 5% of them can complete the primary level education. However, Kazuo Kuroda, JICA Research Institute visiting fellow (and professor of Waseda University), says that the actual situation of children with disabilities is not totally known by international societies due to the various working definitions of a disability. He emphasizes the concept of “inclusive education,” which has become an international trend. Policies towards inclusive education should be not only understood as an equity strategy but also as a quality strategy. Introducing inclusive education will upgrade the standard of education and embrace diversity. It therefore has real potential for all children regardless of whether or not they have any disabilities.

title: Interview  'How to overcome the fragmentation of aid' with Stephan Klingebiel, DIE
text:
Interview  'How to overcome the fragmentation of aid' with Stephan Klingebiel, DIE
While aid fragmentation is a significant dimension of international cooperation, increases in aid donors and aid interventions raise transaction costs; this has become a challenge for both aid providers and partner countries, says Stephan Klingebiel, Head of Department, Bi- and Multilateral Development Cooperation, German Development Institute (DIE). Further, Klingebiel asserts that it is important for the donors to unite for coordinating better aid approaches, such as “global aid architecture,” and harmonize aids, such as “aid programming in EU.” It is more important for partner countries to guide donors to align with partner country systems for effective development cooperation.

title: Interview  'Distinctive characteristics of Japanese aid' with Sakiko Fukuda Parr, the New School
text:
Interview  'Distinctive characteristics of Japanese aid' with Sakiko Fukuda Parr, the New School
Western countries have lead the way in development aid but the rise of emerging donors, including China and India, is changing the landscape of aid. Sakiko Fukuda-Parr, a professor in the Graduate Program in International Affairs at the New School in New York City, looks at the distinctive characteristics of Japanese aid in comparison with those of Western aid and emerging donors. She is a development economist with over 30 years of experience in development cooperation. She recently authored JICA-RI Working Paper No. 130, "Normative Framing of Development Cooperation: Japanese Bilateral Aid between the DAC and Southern Donors" and visited JICA-RI as a distinguished fellow in July 2016.

title: Interview  'Appointed as Chief Economist for ADB' with Yasuyuki Sawada, JICA RI Visiting Fellow
text:
Interview  'Appointed as Chief Economist for ADB' with Yasuyuki Sawada, JICA RI Visiting Fellow
JICA Research Institute Visiting Fellow, Yasuyuki Sawada, who is also a professor at Graduate School of Economics, the University of Tokyo, has been appointed as the Chief Economist at the Asian Development Bank (ADB). He is expected to assume office in the spring of 2017. He talked about his ambitions for joining the ADB.

title: Interview  'Human security concept to confront new threats' with Francisco Rojas Aravena, UPEACE
text:
Interview  'Human security concept to confront new threats' with Francisco Rojas Aravena, UPEACE
Francisco Rojas Aravena, the Rector of the University for Peace, visited JICA-RI in December 2016 and talked about the role of international cooperation in ensuring human security. He says that there exists no other global or holistic security concept to confront new threats for people, such as climate change and natural disasters. Thus, we need a more clear way to resolve these threats by putting people at the center. In the case of Latin America, Rojas says that homicide is the main problem. He argues that international cooperation is crucial to resolve present-day issues and to create the political will to find new solutions.

title: Interview  'Human security brings people into focus' with Des Gasper, Erasmus University Rotterdam
text:
Interview  'Human security brings people into focus' with Des Gasper, Erasmus University Rotterdam
Human security analysis tries to bring a focus on ordinary and vulnerable people into security discussions, says Des Gasper, a professor of Human Development and Public Policy at the International Institute of Social Studies at Erasmus University Rotterdam. He says human security analysis is a part of human development analysis and a way of emphasizing certain questions within human development analysis such as fulfilling basic needs, combining different disciplines, transitioning people’s lives, and subjectivity and interconnection beyond national boundaries. He visited JICA-RI in September 2016 and talked about the difference between "human development" and "human security."

title: Interview  ‘The rise of emerging donors and Japan's aid,’ with Jin Sato, the University of Tokyo
text:
Interview  ‘The rise of emerging donors and Japan's aid,’ with Jin Sato, the University of Tokyo
Japan's aid generally has been rated highly by recipient countries, but the rise of emerging donors has provided an opportunity for Japan to review its aid, says Jin Sato. Sato is a professor of the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia at the University of Tokyo and a JICA-RI visiting fellow. His recent research includes Japan's impact on the evolution of emerging donors and natural resource governance and administration. At JICA-RI, he is researching the history of Japanese ODA and emerging donors. He also says public relations efforts will be necessary for Japan’s ODA to receive a fair evaluation.

title: Interview  'Why Should Rich Nations Help the Poor ' with David Hulme
text:
Interview  'Why Should Rich Nations Help the Poor ' with David Hulme
Ethics and self-interest are the main reasons why rich nations should help the poor, explains David Hulme, professor at the University of Manchester. Hulme argues that granting foreign aid used to be the main approach to international development, but it's declining in significance. So we need to put aid in perspective. That is, not only conventional foreign aid but trade, finance and environmental policy reform, or joined-up policies, must be considered the way forward.

title: Interview  'Japan's foreign aid policy and its effects on India' with Purnendra Jain
text:
Interview  'Japan's foreign aid policy and its effects on India' with Purnendra Jain
India received Japan's first yen loans in 1958. Since then, India has been an attractive aid destination for Japan in both the political and economic senses, says Purnendra Jain, professor of Japanese Studies at the University of Adelaide in Australia. He says India and Japan should cooperate to implement international cooperation in third countries such as Africa and this can be expected to create synergy for more effective and efficient aid, since India and Japan share values, ideas, institutions, rule of law, democracy, human rights and more. He visited JICA-RI as a visiting fellow from June to July, 2016, and talked about Japan's foreign aid policy and its effects on India.

title: Seminar on Japan’s Development Assistance by Richard Manning, former OECD-DAC chair (May 23, 2016)
text:
Seminar on Japan’s Development Assistance by Richard Manning, former OECD-DAC chair (May 23, 2016)
Richard Manning, senior research fellow at the University of Oxford and former OECD-DAC chair, delivered a lecture at the JICA Ichigaya Building on Japan’s approach to development aid, looking back on the interactions between Japan and its DAC partners. He says the strength of Japan's model lies in the promotion of "self-help" efforts, a reasonable balance between multinational and bilateral aid, strong technical expertise backed by strong institutions, and a bilateral delivery system through JICA, among other factors. On the other hand, he noted some challenges, including the need to enhance public understanding and the need to think about stronger evidence-based narratives about what continues to make Japan's approach distinctive and about what needs to be done to improve effectiveness further. He contributed a chapter to the book "Japan's Development Assistance: Foreign Aid and the Post-2015 Agenda," which attempts a critical review of the 60 years of Japanese ODA.

title: Interview  'Impact Evaluation, Education and Development' with Makiko Nakamuro, Keio University
text:
Interview  'Impact Evaluation, Education and Development' with Makiko Nakamuro, Keio University
In Eastern Europe and Central Asia, the governments invested a lot of money into the education sector but it wasn't always successful. Why? This question came up while Makiko Nakamuro was working at the World Bank. Nakamuro, associate professor of faculty of Policy Management at Keio University, says impact evaluation, or evidence-based policymaking, allows us to think about more efficient resource allocation in education. She visited JICA on June 6, 2016, to address a seminar on impact evaluation and education, and was interviewed by JICA-RI.

title: Lecture on 'Smart Cities' by Daniel F. Runde, CSIS (June 8, 2016)
text:
Lecture on 'Smart Cities' by Daniel F. Runde, CSIS (June 8, 2016)
Daniel F. Runde, director, Project on Prosperity and Development, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), delivered a lecture at the JICA Ichigaya Building on smart cities. His lecture was based on the CSIS and JICA-RI joint research project "Transformative Innovation for Sustainable Development and Poverty Reduction: Innovation Ecosystems and Smart Cities." He remarked that CSIS and JICA-RI framed the concept of “smart cities” well in the paper. The concept has three components: effective governance, quality infrastructure and social programs. He emphasized the importance of both adopting new technologies that enable energy efficiency and higher quality of life and enabling capable public administration in building smart cities. He closed his remarks by mentioning recommendations to donor countries and developing countries for building smart cities.

title: Lecture on 'Innovation Ecosystems' by Daniel F. Runde, CSIS (June 8, 2016)
text:
Lecture on 'Innovation Ecosystems' by Daniel F. Runde, CSIS (June 8, 2016)
Daniel F. Runde, director, Project on Prosperity and Development, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), delivered a lecture at the JICA Ichigaya Building on innovation ecosystems. His lecture was based on the CSIS and JICA-RI joint research project "Transformative Innovation for Sustainable Development and Poverty Reduction: Innovation Ecosystems and Smart Cities." He highlighted the example of Fabrication Laboratories (Fab Labs) as innovation ecosystems, and emphasized the importance of international development donors and organizations as catalysts for delivering innovations in developing countries.

title: Interview  'Japan’s Development Assistance' with Richard Manning, former OECD DAC chair
text:
Interview  'Japan’s Development Assistance' with Richard Manning, former OECD DAC chair
Richard Manning, senior research fellow at the University of Oxford and former OECD-DAC chair, visited JICA-RI in May 2016 and talked about his observations on Japan's development approach and its interactions with OECD-DAC. He first shows his surprise at how the Japanese developmental situation has changed since Japan joined the Development Assistance Group. He then says that on the OECD side, there was an unspoken assumption that Japan should look like the average Western donor, and Japan's reaction to this was rather defensive. He points out that Japan could have argued more coherently with other DAC members that its model was well-adapted to Southeast Asia in particular. It is important, he mentioned, to consider how Japan can adapt its model to countries that have weaker institutions, and also, to consider how to help developing countries to spread development spatially inside the country. Finally, he suggested that we should aim for “common interest” rather than “short-term national interest” in the development context. He contributed a chapter to the book "Japan's Development Assistance: Foreign Aid and the Post-2015 Agenda," which attempts a critical review of the 60 years of Japanese ODA.

title: Interview  'Impact evaluation for evidence building' with Emmanuel Jimenez, 3ie
text:
Interview  'Impact evaluation for evidence building' with Emmanuel Jimenez, 3ie
How can we know that a development project is truly effective? Are the outcomes truly achieved by a certain project or policy? Emmanuel Jimenez, executive director of International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie), visited JICA-RI in May, 2016 and talked about the role of impact evaluation and its challenges. He says impact evaluation can show if observed changes and outcomes can be attributed to an intervention itself, such as building schools and promoting health. By building evidence for the impact or the effectiveness of intervention, it can test cause and effect in a rigorous way. Thus, impact evaluation can determine whether a program should be sustained. He has expertise in development economics, welfare economics, public economics and other topics with many years of experience to evaluate the development effectiveness of World Bank projects and programs.

title: Interview  'Digital revolution and open innovation' with Izumi Aizu, Tama University
text:
Interview  'Digital revolution and open innovation' with Izumi Aizu, Tama University
Izumi Aizu, professor at the Institute for InfoSocionomics, Tama University, is one of the key players for promoting online services and the Internet in Japan. He visited JICA-RI in March 2016 and talked about the digital revolution and "open innovation." Open innovation is a concept that encourages companies to use outside sources of innovation to improve efficiency and is often regarded as an opportunity for developing countries. "Open innovation is not giving an answer but just opening a door," he said.

title: "Human Development Report 2015 - Work for Human Development" by Selim Jahan (Mar. 14, 2016)
text:
"Human Development Report 2015 - Work for Human Development" by Selim Jahan (Mar. 14, 2016)
Selim Jahan, Director of Human Development Report Office, UNDP, delivered a lecture at JICA Ichigaya building on the basic messages and findings of the 2015 Human Development Report and policy options.

title: Interview  'Fab labs and social fabrication' with Hiroya Tanaka, Keio University
text:
Interview  'Fab labs and social fabrication' with Hiroya Tanaka, Keio University
Hiroya Tanaka, associate professor, Keio University Shonan Fujisawa Campus (SFC), is the founder of the first fab lab in Japan and he helped advance a fab lab network in Asia. He visited JICA-RI in March 2016 and talked about a fab labs and social fabrication. "Technology itself has no purpose. We have to find a new purpose for solving social issues. So social fabrication means how we can apply new technologies to solve social issues," he said.

title: Interview with Selim Jahan, director of HDR Office, UNDP
text:
Interview with Selim Jahan, director of HDR Office, UNDP
Selim Jahan, director of Human Development Report Office, UNDP, visited JICA-RI in March 2015 and talked about the 2015 Human Development Report "Work for Human Development." "The sustainable development goals and sustainable work are mutually reinforcing and there is a positive linkage between work and sustainable development goals," he said. His areas of expertise include human development, poverty and vulnerability, macroeconomic policies, inequality, inclusive growth, the MDGs and the post-2015 development agenda.

title: Interview with Kenneth King, professor emeritus at the University of Edinburgh
text:
Interview with Kenneth King, professor emeritus at the University of Edinburgh
Kenneth King, professor emeritus at the University of Edinburgh, has conducted research on the "Japaneseness" of Japanese aid, especially in human resource development. As a visiting fellow of the JICA Research Institute, he visited JICA cooperation sites in Cambodia for his research. During his stay in Tokyo, in February and March of 2016, he talked about his observation and insights on the “Japaneseness” of Japanese ODA in education and skills development.

title: Interview with Naoto Kanehira, strategy and operations officer, the World Bank
text:
Interview with Naoto Kanehira, strategy and operations officer, the World Bank
Naoto Kanehira, strategy and operations officer at Budget, Performance Review and Strategic Planning Vice Presidency, the World Bank, has been engaged in work related to industrial competitiveness, promotion of small and medium enterprises, and innovation policy. He visited JICA-RI in December 2015 and talked about the role of innovation for achieving SDGs and ways to eliminate the gap between developing countries and developed countries.

title: Interview with Ludovico Alcorta, director of DPR, UNIDO
text:
Interview with Ludovico Alcorta, director of DPR, UNIDO
Ludovico Alcorta, director of Development Policy, Statistics and Research Branch (DPR) of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), has conducted extensive research on new technologies, innovation and development. He visited JICA-RI in December 2015 and talked about the key message of "Industrial Development Report 2016" and what policy makers should pay attention to with regard to innovation and inclusiveness.

title: Interview with Harounan Kazianga, assistant professor of Oklahoma State University
text:
Interview with Harounan Kazianga, assistant professor of Oklahoma State University
Harounan Kazianga, assistant professor of Economics Spears School of Business, Oklahoma State University, visited JICA-RI in December 2015 and talked about conditional cash transfers. He talked about the role of conditionality, research findings and the policy implications for having conditional cash transfer programs in place.

title: COVID-19 Webinar Series #9 "Understanding the Actual Spread of COVID-19 by Wastewater Surveillance"
text:
COVID-19 Webinar Series #9 "Understanding the Actual Spread of COVID-19 by Wastewater Surveillance"
JICA COVID-19 Webinar Series starting January 2021 brings together various leading health professionals from Japan to share Japan’s knowledge and experience on COVID-19 response and discuss the implications of their work. The webinar is intended primarily for health professionals in low- and middle-income countries.

In the 9th webinar, we focused on “precaution” by wastewater surveillance. Wastewater surveillance is expected to be utilized as an effective surveillance tool to complement traditional surveillance in the presence of unrecognized infections. Three speakers gave an overview of COVID-19 wastewater surveillance in the world, latest research findings and testing methods developed in Japan, and discussed adaptation in low- and middle income countries.

title: Seminar 'At Your Services?: The Promise of Services-Led Development' (December 3, 2021)
text:
Seminar 'At Your Services?: The Promise of Services-Led Development' (December 3, 2021)
Manufacturing-led development has been the traditional model for creating jobs and prosperity. But in the past three decades, the services sector has grown faster than the manufacturing sector in many developing economies. In 2019, the services sector accounted for an average of 55 percent of GDP and 45 percent of employment in developing economies. 

As manufacturing’s share of economies across the development spectrum recedes, can the services sector help low- and middle-income countries catch up with high-income countries, while expanding good job opportunities? A report entitled "At Your Service? The Promise of Services-Led Development" assesses the prospects for services-led development. Its findings and their implications are encouraging for the World Bank Group’s “better jobs for more people” Jobs and Economic Transformation agenda. 

At this seminar, the co-authors of the report shared the main findings.

title: Mochitsuki Pounding rice Rice Cakes 2020
text:
Mochitsuki Pounding rice Rice Cakes 2020
JICA participants enjoyed "Mochitsuki," pounding cooked rice to make "MOCHI" Rice Cakes, on January 17 at the court yard.  Under the instruction of Japanese staff, participants pounding cooked rice with wooden stick in "HAPPI", Japanese traditional work wear. This was their first time to do so, but they did powerfully and wonderfully along with cheering calls "Yoisho, Yoisho" given from surrounding people.

The rice-cake were then cut in pieces by hands, and served with sweet beans paste, soy bean powders, sugar, soy sauce, and strawberry.  Participants enjoyed the traditional japanese delicacy.
